stories.Headline: Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress moves performance reviews to December to accelerate salary increases
stories.Summary:
Nvidia executives held a company wide meeting on November 18 to steady the organization after Jensen Huang resigned. Interim CEO Colette Kress told the hour long meeting that commitments to shareholders and customers remain unchanged. Co founder Chris Malachowsky criticized Huang by saying he hesitated over damage to the value of highest standards. Board chairman Harvey Jones distanced the company from talk of a return for the former chief executive. Management pledged to maintain deals with TSMC and hold the GTC conference next month.

Kress announced that performance reviews normally held each March will move up to December to accelerate salary increases. This change aims to lift employee morale after pay became the most common topic among 700 submitted questions. The company stock currently trades 37 percent below its 52 week high as the organization seeks stability. Harvey Jones reaffirmed the plan to hire a replacement from outside because capable leaders exist beyond the company. Management also pledged to develop next generation chips and complete the acquisition of Hugging Face.

Interim CEO Colette Kress stated that the ambitions of the company remain unchanged despite the leadership transition. Vice president Ian Buck told employees they do not need to worry about the next generation AI chip roadmap. Chairman Harvey Jones said that finding a direct replacement for Huang was unrealistic for the current board. Chris Malachowsky spoke with a breaking voice while criticizing the failure to uphold the highest company standards. These leaders sought to reassure the workforce during a period of significant internal and external instability.

Employee reactions to the possibility of a return for Jensen Huang were mixed according to various reports. One attendee told the Times there was a strong desire for him to return to the company. Another employee told CNBC they did not understand the categorical response while an investigation was still underway. A different person disputed that account and said employees welcomed the transparent communication from the current management. Hedge fund manager Bill Ackman called the board decision a serious governance failure on the platform X.

The company is currently shaken by the resignation of its former chief executive officer, Jensen Huang. This leadership crisis occurs while the company manages its roadmap for artificial intelligence chips and customer commitments. The organization is facing pressure from shareholders and employees regarding pay and the future of its leadership. Internal tensions are high as the board seeks an outside hire to lead the global chip maker. The company continues to operate its business while dealing with the fallout of the executive departure.

Jensen Huang and general counsel Tim Teter are scheduled to testify at a closed door briefing for lawmakers. This briefing will take place the same week as the upcoming Nvidia GTC conference next month. The company must still navigate the investigation mentioned by employees and the criticism from Bill Ackman. It remains open whether the accelerated pay reviews will successfully lift the morale of the shaken workforce. The board has not yet named a permanent successor to replace the former chief executive officer.

stories.Headline: Pearl price jumps 66% as developers schedule FP8 mining upgrade on testnet
stories.Summary:
Pearl price gained nearly 66% over seven days as its market capitalization approached $900 million, according to CoinGecko data reported on Thursday. PEARL traded at $2.34, up nearly 35% over 24 hours, while daily trading volume stood at $58.33 million, placing the cryptocurrency among the 75 largest digital assets. The rally followed Coinbase's introduction of PEARL spot trading on Nov. 13, alongside an announcement covering perpetual futures markets in supported jurisdictions. Cryptocurrency investment firm Syncracy Capital disclosed that it had accumulated a substantial position in PEARL over the past two quarters, citing the network's potential to benefit from investment in AI infrastructure.

Pearl is a layer-1 blockchain that uses matrix multiplication, a mathematical operation central to AI training and inference, to secure its network through proof of useful work. Unlike Bitcoin, whose mining algorithm requires specialized hardware to calculate cryptographic hashes, Pearl allows graphics processing units to earn cryptocurrency rewards while performing calculations that AI models already require. On Nov. 17, developers merged a software update scheduling FP8 activation on Pearl's test network, while the mainnet activation height remains unset. Pearl currently relies on integer-based calculations for mining, and the proposed FP8 upgrade introduces support for eight-bit floating-point calculations, a numerical format commonly used by modern AI inference systems. However, the upgrade initially restricts supported mining hardware to Nvidia's Hopper and Blackwell GPU architectures.

Research firm Kairos Research, which holds PEARL, estimates that approximately two-thirds of the network's existing computational power could become incompatible under the proposed hardware requirements. Its preliminary tests on an Nvidia H100 found that mining through the FP8 implementation reduced AI serving throughput by 20% to 40%, compared with reductions of 30% to 65% under the existing integer-based implementation. The findings contrast with Pearl's expectations of substantially lower computational overhead, although Kairos tested an early software build on a single GPU. A Nov. 2 research report by Blockworks analysts Sam Schubert and Nick Carpinito estimated that fewer than 1% of Pearl's blocks matched genuine AI models, while consumer-grade GPUs accounted for approximately 82% of the network's computational power. Pearl's protocol verifies that the required mathematical operations occurred but does not independently establish whether miners performed them in response to paying customers' requests.

The project has secured at least one commercial integration, as AI infrastructure provider Together AI announced an exclusive partnership with Pearl Research Labs in May, introducing a modified Gemma AI model priced more than 25% below its standard rate through anticipated cryptocurrency mining proceeds. However, Together AI's current product page states that the model is not available on Together's Serverless API. Pearl Research Labs operates its own inference platform, which provides developers with API access to AI models, though public documentation does not quantify its paying customer base or the proportion of mining activity attributable to commercial inference requests. Pearl Research Labs, its team and shareholders collectively reported holding 98 million PEARL.

stories.Headline: ASI Foundry chairman Jimmy Lee promotes physical AI development for the manufacturing industry
stories.Summary:
Jimmy Lee spoke with Seoul Economic Daily on November 17 in Palo Alto, California. He is the chairman of an industrial AI company called ASI Foundry. Lee is a 1.5-generation Korean-American who emigrated to the United States at age 12. He previously served as a state cabinet official and a deputy secretary of commerce. He now promotes the development of physical AI for the manufacturing industry.

Lee served as Virginia's deputy secretary of commerce and a governor's energy advisory council member. He was later appointed as Maryland's special secretary for minority affairs by Governor Larry Hogan. He also worked at the Livingston Group on international trade, development, energy, and small-business matters. ASI Foundry now helps manufacturers combine their data with AI to enter the physical AI market. This technology integrates AI with the physical world, such as machines and Waymo cars.

Jimmy Lee stated that Korea can lead in physical AI because it is a manufacturing powerhouse. He argued that Korean factories hold enormous amounts of data that must be structured for AI. Lee believes that the cost of inaction is greater than the cost of taking action. He said that the Korean government is ahead on vision with policies like Saemangeum. He noted that the world needs 2.5 times more data centers than currently exist.

Lee mentioned that mid-sized and small Korean companies want their data developed for physical AI. He noted that suppliers of parts like screws and pipelines hold the most important data. He believes that shipbuilding, autos, and semiconductors are the key areas where Korea remains most competitive. Residents in the United States sometimes oppose data centers due to noise and wealth gaps. He cited Loudoun County, Virginia, as a place that uses tax revenue to benefit residents.

Lee is the son of Jhoon Rhee, who is known as the godfather of taekwondo. He noted that the United States and China currently lead the AI model market. He mentioned that Chinese models include DeepSeek, Qwen, and Kimi, which he called open engines. He referenced Yann LeCun and Project Tapestry regarding the joint building of common AI models. He also mentioned that Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix lead in high-bandwidth memory.

Lee predicts that AI infrastructure buildout will continue despite Democratic gubernatorial wins in the midterms. He believes Korea could eventually make GPUs if a flywheel ecosystem takes shape. He suggests that data will eventually be exchanged like trade within a global framework. He noted that gas turbines from Doosan have long delivery times of four or five years. The articles leave open how Korea will specifically open its data to remain competitive.

stories.Headline: Grindr launches Edge AI subscription worldwide at $120 a month
stories.Summary:
Grindr Inc. put Edge, a premium subscription built on its own artificial intelligence technology, on sale worldwide on iOS and Android on November 17, 2026, priced in the United States at $120 a month or $70 a week. The West Hollywood company announced the tier through Business Wire at 9:00 a.m. Eastern time. Edge sells three features that Grindr says save users time: a daily set of five curated profiles, estimates of compatibility and of the likelihood of a reply, and a tool that brings past conversations back into view with summaries. The announcement states that Grindr does not use HIV status, last-tested information, vaccination status or Poz tags to power or train the AI behind the product.

The launch closes a test that ran for most of 2026. Edge runs on gAI, the name Grindr gives its proprietary AI technology, and the release says the tier introduces new tools for discovery, compatibility and reconnecting. The compatibility feature identifies patterns in who a person typically reaches out to, including age groups, positions or tribes, using profile information and activity, chats included, where the user consents. The five curated profiles appear as an Edge Recommends carousel when the app opens, mixing newly discovered profiles with past connections and explaining why each person appears, and the blog post puts the daily Discover selection at as many as five profiles. The reconnect tool works in the manner of smart favorites, gathering past conversations with chat summaries.

The release gives the price in a single sentence: $120 USD per month or $70 USD per week in the United States, with market-specific pricing where applicable, and no other market's price is disclosed. George Arison, Grindr's chief executive, said Edge is an important step in making Grindr more personal and advancing the company's premiumization strategy, delivering more value to people while ensuring a continuous, awesome experience for free users. Arison said that by bringing gAI to a new, more curated experience, Grindr is helping people discover the connections they want to meet, understand compatibility before they reach out, and reconnect with someone they may have missed. He called it a differentiated, value-added offering for people who want to get more out of Grindr. AJ Balance, chief product officer, said building Edge meant listening closely to how people actually use Grindr, then designing technology around the key moments where a little more information or a timely nudge can make a real difference.

Balance said the team created an experience that feels intuitive from the moment you open it, while keeping the person, the possibility and the choice to connect at the center. At $70 a week, a subscriber who pays for a full year spends $3,640, against $1,440 on the monthly plan, by PPC Land's calculation, and two weeks on the weekly plan cost $140, already more than a month on the monthly one. The monthly Edge price is about 2.7 times the Unlimited price reported in February and about 5.2 times XTRA, by PPC Land's calculation. Average revenue per paying user was $27.15 a month in the third quarter of 2026, from about 1.4 million paying users, so a single Edge subscriber on the monthly plan pays about 4.4 times that average. The third-quarter shareholder letter set a hard limit that Edge membership may not exceed 1% of Grindr's global monthly active users, with a target of one-third to two-thirds of 1% within three to four years.

The release puts Grindr's audience at nearly 16 million average monthly active users in virtually every country in the world, and on that figure the cap works out to roughly 160,000 subscribers, PPC Land calculates. Grindr's fourth-quarter 2025 results, published on February 26, 2026, described Edge as in testing across Australia and select US and international markets and as the core of its 2027 growth plan. A blog post dated February 3, 2026, in which Grindr announced the pilot, named Australia and New Zealand as the first pilot markets, followed by select US cities and Canada, and listed A-List, Discover and Profile Insights, of which only Insights survived the rename intact. During the pilot, according to Grindr's February post, prices were randomized across eligible users, so different people saw different amounts, and reports of a $500-a-month tier circulated online earlier in the year. On the second-quarter call in August, Arison said Grindr had never tested a $500 price in the United States and that the figure came from a test in Canadian dollars, and by the third-quarter call on November 5 the company had settled on $120, with Arison telling analysts that testing data supported a higher price that Grindr chose not to charge.

Early-access registration opened on October 20 at edge.grindr.com, and nearly 400,000 users signed up within 72 hours, almost four times a first-week goal of 100,000, with early access beginning on November 10. The release says users have clear choices about how gAI uses their information, with data controls available in their Privacy settings, and that Grindr does not use health information like HIV status, last-tested information, vaccination status or Poz tags to power or train gAI features. According to Grindr's launch blog post and an October 27, 2026 post on gAI controls, the controls sit under Privacy Settings, then Sensitive Data, and Grindr began showing the simplified controls to returning and new users in the last week of October. A Personalize gAI Features switch governs whether a person's sensitive data and chat content are used for Insights, Recommendations and Reconnect, and with the switch off those three features do not work for that person and the person does not appear in other users' experiences of them.

A second switch, Contribute to Smarter gAI, governs whether the same data is used to improve future gAI features, and Grindr says turning it off does not affect access to Edge or other gAI features. Grindr's launch post says some Insights about a person may be visible to Edge subscribers who view that person's profile even if the person does not subscribe, and a separate screen, Privacy Settings then Insights, lets each user review the Insights generated about them and delete ones they do not want shown. The launch post says HIV status, last-tested date, testing reminders, the Poz tribe and tag, and vaccination status are excluded from gAI features and from training regardless of a user's settings, while the release's own list is shorter and ends with like, which leaves open whether it is exhaustive. Grindr's October post gives position, ethnicity and user chats as examples of sensitive data where the law protects it, and under the GDPR data on a person's sexual orientation, sex life and health falls into special category data, which can be processed only under narrow conditions such as explicit consent, and Grindr does not cite a legal basis in the release.

In a September 16, 2025 post titled Privacy at the Core of Grindr's gAI Future, Grindr placed AI opt-outs under a section called AI Technology Controls, reached through the Safety & Privacy Center, then Privacy, then Privacy Settings. That post said Grindr would use sensitive personal information, including sexual preferences, chat data and certain tags or tribes, for AI training only with explicit, separate permission, and that health-related data would not be used for AI, advertising or Grindr marketing. A note added to that post and to the February Edge post on November 17 says Grindr has retired the previous AI controls and launched the simplified set. The launch post, written by Balance, says more features and major updates are planned throughout 2027, and that the iOS version uses glass-inspired navigation.

Grindr does not report Edge revenue separately, and the November 17 release does not mention the cap at all. The old privacy path sat inside a broader privacy menu, while the new one names sensitive data directly, and the new personalization switch carries a visibility consequence, since switching it off removes a person from what other users see through Edge's features. The articles leave open whether the release's list of excluded health information is exhaustive, and they give no legal basis for the processing. The articles also leave open how market-specific pricing outside the United States is set.

stories.Headline: Novo Nordisk partners with nference on AI for obesity, diabetes and heart disease
stories.Summary:
Novo Nordisk signed an artificial intelligence partnership with the US-based company nference covering obesity, diabetes, and heart disease, MedWatch reported on 19 November 2026. The collaboration will link Novo’s clinical trial data with real-world data from US hospital networks, according to the report. The agreement also lays the groundwork for the two parties to jointly launch new AI companies. MedWatch described the partnership as a path for Novo to gain new insights into the three disease areas.

They also give no details on the new AI companies that could be launched jointly, such as their number, focus, or timing. Novo’s clinical trial data and the hospital network data are the two named sources the collaboration will connect.

The report frames the deal as groundwork for joint AI companies rather than a finished venture. The articles do not name the Novo or nference executives who signed the agreement or give direct statements from them about the partnership. Responsibility for the collaboration sits with the two companies, Novo Nordisk and nference, which the report identifies as US-based. No further comment from either side is included in the material.

The context given is Novo’s interest in new insights into obesity, diabetes, and heart disease, the areas the partnership covers. The articles do not say what happens next beyond the stated groundwork for jointly launching new AI companies. No timeline, regulatory steps, or further announcements are described. More to follow.

stories.Summary:
Kuaishou Technology reported a significant decline in its adjusted earnings and total revenue during the third quarter of 2026. The company released these financial details on November 19, 2026, through a set of official slides. This downturn occurred primarily because the firm increased its spending on artificial intelligence technologies. These heavy investments weighed heavily on the overall margins of the business during this period. The total revenue for the third quarter of 2026 reached a sum of RMB31.6bn.

This financial result was accompanied by a lower gross margin and a sharp reduction in adjusted earnings. Despite these financial struggles, the company maintained strong user metrics across its various platforms. The firm also reported that its available funds had reached a total of RMB127.2bn. The company is responsible for these results and attributed the lower margins to its strategic AI investment.

Management indicated that the pursuit of advanced technology required a higher level of spending. They suggested that these costs were necessary for the long term growth of the business. The reports imply that the firm is prioritizing technological evolution over immediate short term profitability. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Kim Jae-kyoung says AI finds predictive patterns without knowing why they work
stories.Summary:
The ninth Daesung Haegang Science Forum took place at The Westin Josun Seoul in central Seoul on Thursday, Nov. 19, under the theme "AI Fundamentals and Beyond." It was hosted by the Daesung Haegang Cultural Foundation and organized by Daesung Group, with KAIST and the Korean Society for Biotechnology and Bioengineering as co-organizers. Kim Jae-kyoung, a professor of mathematical sciences at KAIST, said today's AI resembles the astronomer Johannes Kepler. Kepler studied years of celestial observations and worked out that planets travel in elliptical paths, but he could not explain why. Isaac Newton later asked the question again, and the answer he found explained the movement of celestial bodies, falling apples and ocean tides all at once.

Kim said today's AI finds patterns in data and finds functions that predict well, but it does not actually know why that function comes out as a result. He pointed to a study published last year in which simply adding up the known effects of two single-gene changes beat five celebrated AI foundation models at predicting what happens when both genes are changed at once. His own team feeds machines the scientific rules researchers have already established rather than more data, an approach that produced a sleep feature now built into Samsung Electronics' Galaxy Watch. Lee Jae-wook, a professor of computer science and engineering at Seoul National University, said AI chips can now calculate roughly 60,000 times faster than 20 years ago, but the memory that feeds them data has sped up only about 100 times. Engineers call this the memory wall, and it is the main reason high bandwidth memory, the specialty of Korean chipmakers, commands such demand.

Cha Won-chul, a professor of emergency medicine at Samsung Medical Center, described patients carrying copies of their scans from hospital to hospital, paramedics calling 20 hospitals in a row to find a bed, and patient records too long for any doctor to absorb. He said that if he read out everything in a patient's existing chart, they would have to go home, and that he does not have enough tokens for that. Kim Dong-hyuk, a professor at KAIST's Graduate School of Engineering Biology, closed the session on synthetic biology, the field that engineers living cells to do things they cannot do in nature, such as making an ingredient for a malaria drug in yeast instead of extracting it from a plant. He said costs are falling quickly, and one experiment in his lab dropped from about $200 per sample to roughly $20. That lets researchers test far more ideas than before.

Kim Young-hoon, chairman of Daesung Group and honorary chair of the World Energy Council, said in a brief interview before the forum that Korea faces limits in hosting the data centers that AI requires. He said that as it stands, nuclear power is the only alternative, but nuclear power has become a "not in my backyard" issue. He said residents may welcome data centers, but if nuclear power comes with them, he expects there will be backlash. He said that rather than looking for sites at home, it would be the natural course for Daesung Group to go overseas if there is good land. OpenAI's Economic Research team studied more than 580,000 scientific messages from 1,819 scientists in the ChatGPT for Academic Researchers summer pilot and surveyed 251 participants.

OpenAI analyzed 580,186 scientific messages from 1,819 scientists on the ChatGPT for Academic Researchers plan from August 20 to September 22, 2026. The survey ran from September 30 to October 7, with 251 scientists' responses presented in the analysis, and the number of answers varies by question. Surveyed participants estimated that the same work, at the same quality, would have taken 1.9 times as long without AI. 68% of scientists used ChatGPT to develop research ideas, and 98% of those who answered the question about discovery timelines expected AI to accelerate discovery in their field. By default, OpenAI does not use participants' data from the ChatGPT for Academic Researchers program to train its models.

OpenAI used automated classifiers to sort messages by the type of research activity, such as reviewing literature, writing code, or analyzing data, and the research team could see those categories but did not read the underlying messages or ChatGPT's responses. For each scientist, the team calculated the share of their scientific messages in each activity, then averaged those shares, giving every scientist equal weight, and other research activities accounted for less than 1%. OpenAI asked 250 scientists to imagine a discovery that would take 10 years without AI and estimate how long it would take with AI, and respondents could select multiple fields, so field groups overlap. OpenAI identified 367 reasons in 224 written responses from scientists who expected faster discovery, and scientists could give multiple reasons. OpenAI is expanding ChatGPT for Academic Researchers with free access for more than 200,000 researchers around the world.

stories.Headline: InMobi launches AI platform to manage advertising campaigns for small businesses
stories.Summary:
On November 18, 2026, InMobi launched a new platform called InMobi Accelerate. This tool uses seven AI agents to manage advertising campaigns for small and medium businesses. It also serves the agencies that work with these smaller firms. The company announced the product from San Mateo, California, at 7:00 AM Eastern. The launch took place at the Glance Forward event in New York.

The platform manages ads for Google, Meta, Microsoft, TikTok, and ChatGPT from one dashboard. It is available at accelerate.inmobi.com and is free to start. Seven agents act as a business analyst, audience strategist, media planner, copywriter, creative designer, launch engineer, and optimizer. It uses a first-party pixel to report a single cross-channel figure called True ROAS. This data feeds Mobius, a decisioning system unveiled on October 5.

Rohit Dosi is the VP and GM of InMobi Accelerate. He stated that AI agents change the economics of expertise for growing businesses. Dosi said agencies could take on more clients without adding repetitive work. InMobi claims the tool allows businesses to grow without hiring seven specialists. The company says it helps users avoid the slow work of assembling reports.

Small businesses and agencies are the intended users of this self-serve platform. InMobi notes that many advertisers struggle to measure results across different platforms. A NewtonX survey of 800 US small advertisers found only 4% can launch campaigns same-day. Some users may be affected by how True ROAS credits sales across platforms. The system allows users to connect existing accounts and import past results.

InMobi says over 70% of surveyed businesses run campaigns on multiple platforms. Mobius reportedly processes 25 trillion predictions and 200 billion opportunities on an average day. OpenAI opened ChatGPT Ads Manager to US businesses on May 5 and expanded globally by October 21. A separate StackAdapt survey found that only 7% of senior marketers use unified measurement. InMobi previously used Mobius to reach 8.6 million Grocery Outlet shoppers.

Users must approve every plan, creative asset, and budget before any ads go live. Continuous optimization only runs if the advertiser authorizes it within set parameters. The service can be cancelled in one click, and connected accounts remain the advertiser's own. The articles do not list specific pricing beyond the free start or budget cap parameters. It remains unclear how the platform connects to ChatGPT Ads or its specific controls.

stories.Headline: TrendForce attributes falling NAND spot prices to weak smartphone and PC demand and module maker inventory clearance
stories.Summary:
Commodity NAND spot prices fell about 20 percent since the second half of last month. This decline happened while high value products for AI data centers remained firm. Industry sources reported these findings on November 16, 2026. The drop occurred despite a general boom in artificial intelligence memory. Memory chip prices are soaring overall, but the NAND market is moving opposite.

A 512 gigabit NAND wafer dropped 32 percent this quarter to 14.30 dollars. One terabit products fell 19 percent to 24.90 dollars in the same period. Counterpoint Research expects global smartphone shipments to fall 13.9 percent to 1.08 billion units. Gartner says third quarter PC shipments fell 22.4 percent to 55.35 million units. YMTC revenue share reached 14 percent in the second quarter in Wuhan, Hubei.

Bank of America said NAND is most likely to face price correction first. A memory industry official stated that NAND cannot sustain the steep price gains. TrendForce cited weak smartphone and PC demand as main drivers of the drop. They also blamed inventory clearance by module makers for the recent price decline. These experts believe buyers will press harder for discounts in early year negotiations.

Consumers are delaying upgrades because higher memory costs feed into retail prices. Smartphone makers are reducing base storage capacity or charging more for higher capacity. PC makers are drawing down existing inventory rather than placing new memory orders. Large U.S. technology companies are expanding AI data center investment, benefiting enterprise SSDs. These high value products are now in shortage while commodity chips build up.

YMTC is closing in on SK hynix at 19 percent and Samsung Electronics at 28 percent. Older fabrication lines account for 20 to 30 percent of global NAND wafer capacity. These old plants cannot be quickly converted to make advanced high performance enterprise drives. Enterprise SSDs rose to 48 percent of total NAND bit shipments in the second quarter. This is a sharp increase from the 26 percent recorded a year earlier.

TrendForce expects enterprise SSD contract prices to rise 15 to 20 percent this quarter. Bank of America expects smartphone and PC NAND prices to fall 5 to 10 percent. Nvidia unveiled technology using SSDs to handle data generated during AI inference more efficiently. The articles leave open if spot prices have translated into lower contract prices yet. Future conditions depend on if AI growth can offset weakness in commodity chips.

stories.Headline: Sources expect Anthropic to allocate under 20% of its IPO shares to retail investors
stories.Summary:
Sources expect Anthropic's allocation of shares for retail investors in its blockbuster initial public offering to fall below 20 percent, according to the Financial Times. Retail buyers have historically received between 5 percent and 10 percent of the shares in large initial public offerings. The report, published on 19 November 2026, cites people described as sources for the expected allocation figure. The article itself sits behind a subscription paywall, so the full details of the offering are not available in the text provided.

The expected allocation matters because it would set the share of the offering that ordinary investors could buy rather than institutions. The historical range of 5 percent to 10 percent for large listings gives a benchmark against which the expected Anthropic figure can be compared. The report does not give the total size of the offering, the price of the shares or the date on which trading would begin. It also does not name the banks or advisers working on the transaction.

The sources cited by the Financial Times are responsible for the expected allocation figure, and the article attributes the expectation to them rather than to Anthropic itself. The report does not include any statement from Anthropic or from any underwriter about how the shares would be divided. No named executive or official is quoted in the available text. The article carries no comment from the company on the expected retail share.

The context is that retail investors have historically received a small slice of large initial public offerings, at 5 percent to 10 percent of the shares. The report does not say what happens next, such as when the allocation would be confirmed or when the shares would list. It also does not say whether the expected figure could change before the offering is completed. More detail may emerge as the transaction proceeds.

stories.Headline: Redbox joins NVIDIA Inception to speed AI analysis of menstrual blood data for health and drug discovery
stories.Summary:
Redbox Co., Ltd., the company behind the bio-intelligence business of the NPO Red Box Japan, announced on November 19, 2026, that it had joined the NVIDIA Inception Program, a global startup support program run by NVIDIA Corporation for companies working on advanced technologies such as AI and data science. The announcement said the participation would let the company use NVIDIA's ecosystem to speed up research and development that analyzes biological data, including menstrual blood, with AI. Redbox said it aims to build the data it has accumulated into a foundation for extending healthy life expectancy by ten years, and to use it in ways that also help drug discovery research. The program gives participating startups access to NVIDIA's technical knowledge and training, preferential treatment for hardware and software, and networks with investors and partner companies.

Redbox works on bio-intelligence research and development that comprehensively analyzes biological data, including menstrual blood, starting from support for access to sanitary products. The company said menstruation is a valuable source of information that periodically reflects conditions inside a woman's body, and that large-scale data processing and the use of AI technology are essential to analyze such data at a high level and help each person understand her own health. Through the participation, Redbox said it will build a data analysis infrastructure using GPUs and set up a structure to develop and verify AI models more efficiently. Under the NVIDIA ecosystem, the company plans to build foundation data for extending healthy life expectancy by ten years by analyzing biological data obtained continuously along the menstrual cycle with AI, so that changes in the body and signs of future health risks can be captured.

Redbox also plans to combine its real-world data with AI drug discovery, a field in which the use of AI for protein structure prediction and molecular design has advanced rapidly and shown the potential to greatly shorten the time and cost of finding drug candidates. The company said that improving the accuracy of such AI models and connecting them to medicines that reach actual patients requires biological data obtained in daily life, and that it accumulates data gained continuously along the menstrual cycle as its own real-world data. By combining this data with AI drug discovery technology, Redbox aims to contribute to the search for drug targets and the development of new treatments and medicines in the field of women's health, where research data has been insufficient. It said it will also use the same data and AI analysis technology in supplement development, reading nutritional trends linked to the menstrual cycle and changes in physical condition and developing supplements based on scientific evidence for each person's condition.

Representative Ryoichi Oguma said the company will use the Inception Program to further accelerate the bio-intelligence research and development built on its own real-world data, including menstrual blood, and the analysis of that data. He said Redbox will act not merely as a provider of data and technology but as a partner that creates practical value in both society and business together with research institutions, pharmaceutical companies and partner companies. He said the company will work on a foundation model of multimodal AI that integrates biological data, physical condition records and life logs, a data infrastructure in a secure sovereign environment that takes privacy into account, and a user experience that lets each person understand her own body and turn that understanding into action. Through these efforts, he said, Redbox aims to contribute to AI drug discovery and supplement development and to realize a society that extends healthy life expectancy by ten years.

REDBOX BIO is a next-generation bio-intelligence service that combines and analyzes three kinds of biological data: menstrual blood, blood and facial stratum corneum, or ceramide, to understand each person's body from multiple angles. By continuously accumulating and learning biomarkers such as proteins, metabolites, hormone rhythms and skin lipids, it aims to provide personalized health management in which understanding of one's body deepens as data increases, rather than ending with a single test. The service is set to cover a wide range from athletes' conditioning to beauty, daily performance and longevity, and a women-only model called Model X is scheduled to be provided in 2027. Redbox said it will continue to deepen cooperation with companies, local governments, educational institutions and research institutions, and to use NVIDIA's ecosystem while advancing the building of a data foundation for extending healthy life expectancy, AI drug discovery and supplement development, as well as healthcare services that let each person understand her own body and manage her health proactively.

stories.Headline: Linq raises $90 million led by Andreessen Horowitz to build AI agent infrastructure
stories.Summary:
Linq, an infrastructure platform for AI agents based in San Francisco, announced on November 18, 2026 that it has raised $90 million in new funding led by Andreessen Horowitz, with continued participation from TQ Ventures, Mucker Capital, and Abstract, and new participation from Anthos and Left Lane Capital. Ben Horowitz, cofounder and general partner at Andreessen Horowitz, will join Linq's board of directors. The company was founded by Elliott Potter, who serves as CEO, Patrick Sullivan, who serves as CTO, and Jared Mattsson, who serves as President. Linq said its messaging product has already processed more than 1 billion messages, and it counts DoorDash, Town, Tomo, and hundreds of other companies as providers. The funding will support continued investment in messaging and the expansion of Linq's product lineup through its own software, hardware infrastructure, and strategic partnerships.

Linq's computer use offering gives agents access to physical computing infrastructure to interact with software and complete tasks, and HD Calling for Agents adds voice calling to the platform. As an Apple Messaging Service Provider, Linq can help more enterprises launch and scale customer-facing agents on the same channel. The company cited Cloudflare reporting that more than half of internet traffic is no longer human, with AI agent requests on its network up more than 1,700% in a year. Horowitz said agents will communicate and get work done just like people do, and that Linq gives agents the infrastructure to do both at scale. Potter said clicking through five screens to make a payment will become two words to an agent, pay rent, and that Linq helps developers build customer-facing agents that use human tools to do human work.

Aryan Shah, Head of AI research at DoorDash, said the best AI experiences fit naturally into people's lives, and that Linq gives DoorDash the messaging infrastructure to bring ordering into a familiar conversation so customers can go from deciding what they want to placing an order in one thread. Linq describes itself as the platform for building AI agents, bringing together messaging and an expanding set of tools for interacting with the world, helping developers spend less time assembling infrastructure and more time building products. The company said messaging was its first product and remains a core part of its growing AI infrastructure platform. The announcement framed the shift as one in which people will describe what they need and agents will get it done, following the internet giving every business a website and the iPhone giving every business an app. Companies can learn more at linqapp.com.

stories.Headline: Google Cloud deploys AMD Epyc CPUs to power its TPU systems
stories.Summary:
The Motley Fool published an article on November 15, 2026, by Harsh Chauhan, arguing that Advanced Micro Devices could be the best artificial intelligence stock to buy amid a sell-off. The PHLX Semiconductor Sector index had declined 12% over the past three months, and AMD was caught up in that vortex with significant volatility. Concerns about the sustainability of artificial intelligence infrastructure spending, which has been key to the semiconductor sector's growth, drove the weakness. AMD's stock fell $51.24, or 8.75%, to $534.06 as of 4:00 PM ET on 11/13/26 on the NASDAQ. The article said the recent weakness opened a great opportunity for investors to buy a top stock at an attractive valuation.

AMD's data center revenue jumped 97% year over year in Q3 to $8.5 billion, driven by tremendous demand for its Epyc server central processing units from hyperscalers and AI companies. Alphabet's Google Cloud division expanded its partnership with AMD to deploy its 5th-generation Epyc server CPUs, security fabric, and x86 software to power its cloud Tensor Processing Unit systems. AMD Epyc will serve as the foundation for Google's TPUs, allowing users to run inference applications. Google Cloud reported a backlog of $561 billion at the end of the third quarter, and the tech giant expects to recognize half of that backlog in the next two years. AMD expects revenue to increase by more than 80% in 2027, fueled by healthy growth in the data center business, where it sees the server CPU total addressable market jump to $220 billion by 2030.

The article's author, Harsh Chauhan, wrote that he would not be surprised to see AMD embark on a stunning long-term rally. He said AMD is emerging as one of the most important players in the AI chip ecosystem. He noted that AMD has partnerships with major hyperscalers and AI companies, including OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta Platforms, Microsoft, and others, in the data center segment. He wrote that these customers should ensure solid long-term revenue growth for AMD, which is precisely what analysts are expecting. Chauhan disclosed that he has no position in any of the stocks mentioned.

The Motley Fool has positions in and recommends Advanced Micro Devices, Alphabet, Meta Platforms, and Microsoft. The article said the $52.2 billion revenue estimate for 2026 points to a 51% jump over last year, and the forecast for 2027 and 2028 is also quite solid. Analysts expect AMD's EPS to grow by nearly 70% annually over the long run, and AMD trades at 33 times forward earnings. Assuming AMD clocks even 50% earnings growth in 2029 and 2030, its EPS could reach $57.53 by the end of the decade, using 2028's projected EPS of $25.57 as the base. A price-to-earnings ratio of 20 at that time, in line with the tech-focused Nasdaq-100 index's forward P/E, would send AMD's shares to $1,150 in just over four years, twice AMD's current price.

The article noted that the past few months haven't been pretty for semiconductor stocks, as evidenced by the 12% decline in the PHLX Semiconductor Sector index over the past three months. It said AMD's data center segment has incredible room for growth and that Alphabet is poised to spend aggressively on its cloud computing infrastructure. The article stated that AMD is therefore going to be a direct beneficiary of Alphabet's enormous spending. It said AMD is well-positioned to capitalize on the massive server CPU opportunity. The article added that AMD's revenue growth will filter down to the bottom line as well.

The article said opportunistic investors should capitalize on the recent weakness in the semiconductor sector and buy the stock for long-term gains. It said the Motley Fool Stock Advisor analyst team just identified what they believe are the 10 best stocks for investors to buy now, and Advanced Micro Devices wasn't one of them. The article cited Netflix making that list on December 17, 2004, when $1,000 invested would now be worth $335,171. It also cited Nvidia making the list on April 15, 2005, when $1,000 invested would now be worth $1,000,640. The article said Stock Advisor's total average return is 823%, compared to 208% for the S&P 500, with returns as of November 15, 2026.

stories.Headline: IEC proposes Total Contribution framework to assess AI data center sustainability
stories.Summary:
The International Electrotechnical Commission proposed a broader way to judge the sustainability of AI data centers, according to an announcement dated November 17. The IEC issued its Clean Green Data Centres Strategic Position Paper and Leadership Briefing. The proposal introduces a “Total Contribution” framework. That framework considers a facility’s environmental footprint alongside its relationship with the electricity grid, economic productivity and public services. The central idea is that a data center should be assessed as part of a wider system.

The IEC has established a Strategic Standards Group on Data Centres to develop consistent metrics, reporting protocols and assurance mechanisms. The announcement does not establish a completed global scoring formula or a binding requirement that every data center adopt zero-water cooling. The IEC already publishes ISO/IEC 30134-2:2026, which defines PUE and its measurement, calculation and reporting. A PUE of 1.2 means the facility consumes 20% more energy than its IT equipment alone. The framework spans four dimensions: energy and grid integration, environmental and resource stewardship, economic and digital productivity, and societal and regional resilience.

The IEC described the forthcoming paper in an earlier contribution to ITU’s AI for Good platform as a way to identify sustainability and safety gaps in standardization. It emphasized treating data centers as active participants in energy systems and examining cooling, water use, electronic waste and lifecycle emissions. The IEC’s announcement highlights liquid and immersion cooling, direct-current power distribution and power quality for AI infrastructure as areas for standards development. The report’s ambition is to make those relationships visible. Turning that ambition into comparable, verifiable outcomes is the work ahead.

The IEA’s Powering Artificial Intelligence report says active management of computing loads remains rare. Many operators serve third parties and have limited visibility into or control over the work running inside their facilities. The IEA identifies standardized information exchange across computing customers, infrastructure providers and electricity networks as important to unlocking flexibility. The U.S. Department of Energy’s data center water-efficiency guidance illustrates a liquid-cooled system that ultimately transfers heat to a cooling tower. A large facility with an excellent PUE can still place substantial demand on a constrained grid.

Power Usage Effectiveness measures total facility energy divided by the energy used by IT equipment. Lower overhead can indicate more efficient cooling and power delivery, but the ratio does not reveal the facility’s absolute electricity demand or the carbon intensity of its power supply. Two facilities with similar ratios can also have very different water requirements or opportunities to reuse heat. Liquid cooling does not by itself establish that a facility consumes no water. A closed equipment loop can coexist with evaporative heat rejection elsewhere in the system.

The next phase will determine how the proposed framework becomes consistent reporting and assurance that operators, utilities and policymakers can use. The difficult next step is making the four dimensions comparable. A credible assessment needs to show where impacts occur, who receives the benefits and how claims are measured. Reporting needs to define its boundaries clearly enough for readers to understand what a water-saving claim covers. The useful evidence would show what demand can change, for how long and under which service commitments.

stories.Headline: Treasury and White House officials consider requiring US firms to label use of Chinese AI models
stories.Summary:
The Treasury Department and White House science officials discussed requiring US companies to post website notices when using Chinese AI models. Reuters reported this plan on Wednesday, November 19, 2026, as a way to discourage reliance on these models. The proposal would label American adopters like Airbnb but would not impose new restrictions on Chinese developers. No formal rulemaking, text, deadline, or penalty has been announced or enacted by the government yet. The aim is to use reputational costs to name and shame companies that rely on Chinese AI.

The plan would require labels for companies like Airbnb, Anysphere, and DoorDash that use models from developers like Alibaba or Moonshot. House committees sent letters to Airbnb and Anysphere on April 29, and to DoorDash on July 31, 2026. DoorDash was asked for information by August 14 to reduce reliance on models developed in the PRC. Pinterest uses Qwen models for chatbots, and Anysphere's Cursor Composer 2 builds on the Kimi model from Moonshot AI. These labels would not show if data goes to China or if models run on US infrastructure.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent floated the disclosure idea in July and mentioned sanctioning Chinese firms that stole intellectual property. Michael Kratsios, confirmed March 25, 2025, directs the Office of Science and Technology Policy, which issued an April memo. House China Select Committee Chairman John Moolenaar welcomed the report, calling disclosure an important step in managing risks. Moolenaar warned that models hosted on US servers can still carry vulnerabilities that the adopter did not choose. He also sponsored the No Adversarial AI Act, H.R. 4142, which was introduced on June 25, 2025.

Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky said the company uses Alibaba's Qwen models for its customer service agent, which uses 13 models. Chesky stated in May 2026 that Airbnb does not buy from Alibaba or provide data to Chinese companies. Luma AI CEO Amit Jain told Semafor there was no evidence of change among companies using Chinese models. Booz Allen Hamilton found Qwen3-Coder added 130 percent more vulnerabilities under a US government persona than a neutral one. These findings affect US companies that use open-weight models to save money on infrastructure and development costs.

Yicai reported in September that seven Chinese models rank in the top 10 on OpenRouter by call volume. Epoch AI estimated in May that open-weight models lag closed models by about four months on average. Mozilla's September 15 report put the gap at 4.4 months, while other Chinese models trail by 14 months. Moonshot's Kimi K3 scored 57 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index but had a 51 percent hallucination rate.

China's 2017 National Intelligence Law requires organizations to cooperate with intelligence work, though some dispute its enforcement. The government must decide if mandatory labels constitute compelled speech under Zauderer v. Office of Disciplinary Counsel or NIFLA v. Becerra.

It remains unsettled whether a notice saying a product uses a Chinese model is factual or a political message. Companies may use ML-BOM standards like CycloneDX, ECMA-424, or SPDX, but these rely on free-text strings for lineage. The articles leave open whether the Treasury will move into formal rulemaking or keep the labels voluntary. It is unclear if the administration will pursue de facto bans on foreign open-source models in the future.

stories.Headline: FBI warns hackers use Artex AI tool to automate network breaches in under three hours
stories.Summary:
The FBI warned that hackers are using an autonomous AI tool called Artex to launch cyberattacks globally and across the United States. These malicious actors have targeted various industries in recent months, including government, defense, tech, phone, internet companies, and law firms. The agency issued a flash cybersecurity advisory on November 13 to alert businesses and government organizations about these escalating AI-assisted threats. Cybercriminals and state-aligned groups have used this software to automate attacks and gain privileged network access in under three hours. The FBI says these intrusions have occurred since the tool first made its public debut in July of this year.

The framework requires connections to frontier large language models from OpenAI and Anthropic, as well as open-source or non-U.S. models. It targets security flaws like weak protections and stolen passwords to breach networks in South Korea and the United States. Hackers used Artex to access Microsoft 365 cloud environments of at least 2,250 customers of the IT company ConnectWise. In South Korea, the tool targeted financial institutions and stole the personal data of at least 68,000 people due to weak defenses. The tool also breached Barracuda by finding an exposed credential from a third-party vendor that the company had not revoked.

The FBI stated that AI makes sophisticated attacks faster and easier to automate, which makes them more difficult for organizations to detect. Federal investigators noted that Artex intrusions are noisy because they generate reams of traffic and data that trigger defensive alerts. The agency warned on X that the tool allows attackers with limited technical expertise to carry out complex, specialist operations. Barracuda's chief information security officer, Arve Kjoelen, said defenders relying on spotting activity often arrive after the attacker has finished. A spokesperson for ConnectWise did not respond to requests for comment regarding the claims made by the FBI.

Microsoft identified a China-aligned threat actor known as Storm-0940 as the group behind the Artex-assisted campaigns targeting hundreds of organizations. The breach at Barracuda affected stores of credentials used to collect data, though the company cannot rule out customer access. Victims include the financial industry in South Korea and customers of the IT management giant ConnectWise who suffered data theft. Other affected entities include the 178 organizations whose websites were hit by a separate supply-chain attack involving the platform Optimizely. This separate incident involved 188 compromised scripts that could potentially capture sensitive information entered by visitors to those various websites.

Artex was originally developed as an open-source penetration-testing platform designed to identify security weaknesses in applications and computer networks. The tool relies on rapidly scanning a victim's network for signs of weakness before exploiting simple bugs to gain a foothold. Recent reports of banking disruptions at Wells Fargo, Bank of America, and JPMorgan Chase were not linked to these cyberattacks. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin attributed those specific outages to ageing computer infrastructure rather than malicious activity from AI hacking tools. JPMorgan Chase blamed a software bug for its problems, while Microsoft attributed its own disruption to various server issues.

The developer of Artex made the software closed-source to prevent further attacks, but the FBI says the open-source version remains accessible. Researchers recently found hundreds of publicly exposed Artex systems online without passwords, including the system used to target South Korea. The FBI continues to warn that the tool's ability to automate reconnaissance presents a significant challenge for traditional cybersecurity defenses. It remains unclear how many customers were affected by the Barracuda breach because the company's logs were not detailed enough. The articles leave open whether other organizations have been compromised by the circulating open-source version of the Artex tool.

stories.Headline: SemiFive and Preferred Networks stack DRAM on logic to create an AI inference chip alternative to HBM
stories.Summary:
South Korea's SemiFive and Japan's Preferred Networks collaborated to develop a new AI inference chip. These two companies showcased their joint effort known as the MN-Core L2000 project at the SC26 event in Chicago. This announcement took place on November 19, 2026, according to the report from Taipei. The project aims to provide a different approach to memory integration for artificial intelligence hardware. The design requires stacking DRAM directly above a logic die to improve efficiency.

This vertical arrangement changes the conventional 2.5D package layout where processors and HBM sit side by side. By moving the memory on top of the logic, the companies offer a viable alternative to high bandwidth memory. This structural shift is intended to optimize how data moves within the AI inference chip. The development is led by SemiFive and Preferred Networks, who are both seeking better hardware performance.

While the provided text does not include direct quotes, the companies presented the MN-Core L2000 as a solution for inference needs. They are positioning this technology to compete with the standard layouts used in current data center technology. The partnership combines South Korean and Japanese engineering to challenge existing semiconductor packaging norms. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Chinese chip firms import equipment via Singapore to bypass US export controls
stories.Summary:
Chinese semiconductor companies imported large volumes of manufacturing equipment from Singapore between January and July of this year to evade United States export controls. These imports reached 3.456 billion dollars across the production hubs of Shanghai, Beijing, and Anhui, which is double the amount recorded during the same period last year. This strategic shift caused the share of imports from the United States to plunge from 16.0 percent to 4.3 percent. The procurement network has expanded beyond back-end processes to include front-end tools like etching and deposition equipment.

The shift requires a reliance on Singapore-routed tools, including 1.9344 billion dollars in chemical vapor deposition equipment and 405.68 million dollars in physical vapor deposition tools. Imports of etching equipment rose 33 percent to 2.3376 billion dollars, while mounting and bonding tools increased fivefold to 6.39 million dollars. In Anhui Province, where ChangXin Memory Technologies is headquartered, the Singapore share of heat-treatment equipment soared from 3.9 percent in 2022 to 58.5 percent. These tools target the MR-MUF packaging process used by SK Hynix to lead the high-bandwidth memory market.

Analysts from the Korea Institute for International Economic Policy and university professors are responsible for these findings. Kim Hyung-jun stated that core equipment likely used circumvention channels because direct supplies from major companies were blocked. Bae Young-ja noted that circumvention trade through Southeast Asia expanded after United States controls tightened around 2022. Industry officials added that while Chinese memory currently lags South Korea by one to two generations, a strong domestic market could close that gap quickly.

This trend follows United States export controls that took full effect around 2022 to limit China's access to advanced logic chips. Singapore is now viewed as a substantive base for supplying core equipment, specifically through firms like ASMPT. ChangXin Memory Technologies is reportedly mass-producing its fifth-generation HBM3E product using these acquired technologies. The market now watches to see if the United States will tighten controls on these Southeast Asian circumvention channels.

stories.Headline: TradingView compares semiconductor stocks Onto Innovation and KLA Corporation for investors
stories.Summary:
TradingView published a report on November 19, 2026, comparing semiconductor stocks Onto Innovation and KLA Corporation. The article analyzes which company offers a better growth opportunity for investors. Both firms provide inspection, metrology, and process-control equipment to chipmakers. They help manufacturers improve yields and manage complex processes. The semiconductor industry is currently booming due to AI and advanced packaging.

Fortune Business Insights estimates the global metrology and inspection market will grow from $16.26 billion in 2026 to $29.57 billion by 2034. Onto Innovation reported third-quarter revenue of $410 million and a backlog exceeding $1.3 billion. KLA reported fiscal first-quarter revenue of $4.14 billion and $1.34 billion in free cash flow. KLA ended September 2026 with $4.74 billion in cash and $5.72 billion in debt. Onto's fourth-quarter revenue outlook is between $430 million and $450 million.

KLA management expects the wafer fabrication equipment market to exceed $200 billion in 2027 and $220 billion by 2030. They target returning over 90 percent of free cash flow to shareholders through 2030. Onto expects Dragonfly platform revenue to increase more than 80 percent in 2026. Onto also expects growth in advanced logic, DRAM, and NAND nodes to exceed 35 percent in 2027. KLA aims for a gross margin of 63 to 64 percent in 2027.

Zacks Investment Research ranks KLA as a Buy and Onto Innovation as a Hold. Onto faces risks from high customer concentration, as four customers provided 57.1 percent of nine-month revenue. Taiwan and South Korea accounted for 58.9 percent of Onto's sales. KLA expects China revenue to decline to the low-20 percent range by 2027. Onto's stock plunged 32.7 percent in three months, while KLA stock lost 22 percent.

The market is driven by AI accelerators, HBM demand, and 2.5D and 3D integration. Onto's R&D investment rose to $45.1 million in the third quarter from $32.5 million previously. Semilab USA recorded a $2.8 million operating loss in the quarter. Onto recorded a $40.8 million unrealized loss on its Rigaku investment. KLA's process control services revenue grew 14 percent due to a larger installed base.

KLA expects advanced packaging revenue to reach approximately $1.1 billion in 2027. Onto expects Dragonfly G5 front-end inspection applications to provide more opportunities in 2027. KLA plans annual capital expenditures between $600 million and $800 million for capacity expansion. Fab construction delays and infrastructure constraints could extend industry growth cycles into 2028. The report leaves open whether Onto's backlog converts to revenue and if margins remain sustainable.

stories.Headline: Kulicke and Soffa beats Q3 estimates and guides Q4 revenue above consensus on AI packaging demand
stories.Summary:
Kulicke and Soffa reported revenue for calendar Q3 2026, its fiscal Q4 2026, that beat Wall Street expectations, with sales up 131% year on year to $410.3 million against an S&P analyst consensus of $377.7 million, an 8.6% beat. The company also posted non-GAAP profit of $1.52 per share, which was 6.3% above the $1.43 consensus, and adjusted operating income of $96.5 million against analyst estimates of $93.23 million, a 3.5% beat at a 23.5% margin. Its operating margin came in at 21.2%, up from 0.5% in the same quarter last year, while inventory days outstanding fell to 101 from 120 in the previous quarter. The results were reported on 19 November 2026, and the company's market capitalization stood at $3.51 billion.

For the next quarter, Q4 CY2026, Kulicke and Soffa guided revenue to $410 million at the midpoint, which is above analyst estimates of $380 million and 7.9% higher than what analysts were expecting. It also guided adjusted EPS to $1.65 at the midpoint for Q4 CY2026, above analyst estimates of $1.43. Management said the outlook rests on expectations that AI-driven data center expansion and broader adoption of advanced packaging will remain robust, and it believes its expanded portfolio in thermal compression bonding and hybrid bonding positions it for technology transitions in memory and logic chips. The company plans to ship more than twice as many TCB systems as in the prior year, and it expanded its manufacturing footprint in Singapore to triple advanced solutions capacity, with factory utilization above 90%.

CEO Raj Talluri said the company expects to ship more than twice as many TCB systems as in the prior year, reflecting plans to increase capacity and respond to growing customer demand, while also acknowledging ongoing supply chain and investment requirements. Management attributed the quarter's performance to widespread demand in wire bonding, major traction in advanced solutions and improved operational leverage amid technology transitions, and it reported that approximately 75% of semiconductor package units deployed in data centers still rely on wire bonding. The company saw advanced solutions revenue nearly double over the past year, driven by adoption of fluxless thermal compression bonding and the launch of new panel-level packaging systems. Its wedge segment, which serves automotive and industrial markets, benefited from improving demand in power semiconductors and electric vehicle-related applications, with management noting sequential growth and signs of cyclical recovery even though these markets are not yet at long-term averages.

Investors reacted negatively despite the beat, as they scrutinized the sustainability of recent growth and the cyclical nature of the core businesses, and the stock traded at $63.03, down from $66.99 just before the earnings. Management was cautious about visibility beyond the next couple of quarters, citing the cyclical nature of the core wire bonding business, ongoing supply chain constraints and uncertainties in end-market demand, particularly outside of data center and memory. It also recognized that the timing of large panel tool adoption could be uneven, depending on customer readiness and technical challenges related to scaling. In upcoming quarters, attention will focus on the ramp and adoption of panel-level and hybrid bonding systems, sustained utilization and demand for wire bonding as AI infrastructure buildouts continue, and signs of recovery in automotive and industrial segments.

stories.Headline: Turkish regulator imposes interim measures on Google over AI news licensing terms
stories.Summary:
The Turkish Competition Authority announced on 2 November 2026 that the Competition Board had opened an investigation into Google's "AI Overviews" and "AI Mode" features. The Board imposed interim measures on Google by a decision of 8 October 2026 under Article 9(4) of Law No 4054 on the Protection of Competition. The Board's concern is twofold: that Google discriminates among comparable news publishers when selecting and licensing their content for its AI features, and that the terms on which that content is used are unfair. AI Overviews and AI Mode went live in Türkiye on 18 February 2026. The Board opened a preliminary inquiry on 27 August, inspected Google's Turkish subsidiary on 1 September and decided, unanimously, on 8 October.

Google has three months to comply, with daily fines thereafter, and may seek judicial review in Ankara. Google's "search generative AI control", a Search Console setting that lets a site withhold its content from AI features without, on Google's account, affecting its ranking elsewhere, was announced on 3 June 2026, the day the CMA's conduct requirement was published. That setting was tested with UK sites first and reached all sites worldwide on 31 August 2026. Google's News AI pilot, announced on 10 December 2025 and said by Google to cover more than 400 publications by October 2026, pays selected publishers for enhanced content used to develop AI features. The global template contains a most-favoured-customer clause that the Turkish version omits.

The Board found a strong suspicion of two abuses under Article 6: discrimination among comparable publishers, both in the selection of sources for AI answers and in the offer and negotiation of contracts, and the imposition of unfair trading conditions. It noted that the same facts may serve both theories. Google must not discriminate among equivalent publishers on criteria that are not objective, transparent and pre-determined. Google must negotiate in good faith with publishers that seek a contract, on objective, verifiable and transparent criteria reflecting the scope and intensity of use, user engagement and the effect on traffic, visibility and advertising revenue. Google must not penalise in ranking, visibility, indexing or traffic a publisher that declines a contract or its terms.

Google must supply publishers periodically with verifiable data on how their content is used and what engagement and traffic it generates. Google must make the AI opt-out exercisable independently of visibility and indexing in other Google services. Google must not worsen existing contracts or apply divergent terms in new ones, and must report compliance to the Authority. On the Board's redacted figures, search engines account for a substantial share of Turkish news sites' traffic, highest for publishers with weaker brands, and Google's share of that search-referred traffic is consistently high. The Board concludes that Google is an unavoidable trading partner for news publishers.

The Board also records that AI referrals account for less than 0.01% of publishers' traffic. The Board found that tying a publisher's choice about AI use to its visibility in Search limited publishers' ability to refuse. The Board found that the opt-out arrived six and a half months after the features did. The Board found that the opt-out's existence does not settle the matter, since not using it is no evidence of a free choice where the consequences for ranking are not predictable. Examining the global template and the Turkish version, the Board found that Google alone decides which publishers are offered a contract, that the text is standard and non-negotiable, and that the fee is derived from brand value and third-party traffic data by an undisclosed method.

The Board found that the licence is worldwide, sublicensable and extends to training, that there is a single payment with no commitment to use the content or send traffic, and that attribution and linking are owed only "to the extent provided to similarly situated partners" and "where reasonably practicable". The Board observes that publishers signed quickly, which shows consent, not competitive terms. The Board derives the unfair-trading-conditions theory from the general prohibition in Article 6 of Law No 4054, noting that the examples listed in Article 6 are not exhaustive. The Board adopts, almost verbatim, the Commission's test from Apple Music Streaming: trading conditions are unfair where they are imposed by a dominant undertaking on its trading partners, harm the interests of those partners or of third parties, including consumers, and are not necessary to achieve a legitimate objective or go beyond what is necessary for it.

As in Apple, the Board adds that a finding of unfair conditions suffices and that no separate inquiry into a restriction of competition is required. The Board had said a few paragraphs earlier that competition-law intervention against unfair terms presupposes conduct that is not isolated and that produces appreciable "restrictive effects on the market". Article 9(4) permits interim measures that preserve the situation prior to the infringement, yet a duty to negotiate on value-reflecting criteria and to supply usage data creates obligations that did not previously exist. That is likely to be Google's first argument before the administrative court.

The Ankara 9th Administrative Court's Trendyol judgment states that an interim measure may neither punish the undertaking nor put complainants in a better position than before the alleged infringement, and may not substitute for the final decision. The court annulled the non-discrimination order for want of any analysis of whether the sellers concerned were in comparable situations. The Google decision cites that judgment for its standard of proof, not for its ceiling. More to follow.

stories.Headline: SK Hynix invests 1.4 trillion won to support domestic semiconductor suppliers
stories.Summary:
SK Hynix announced that high-bandwidth memory helped push South Korean semiconductor exports to 42.8 percent of total exports from January to October. The company reported record third-quarter revenue of 104.6155 trillion won and an operating profit of 83.3338 trillion won during that period. South Korea became the fourth country to surpass one trillion dollars in annual exports after the United States, Germany, and China. Semiconductor exports jumped 257.5 percent in October alone to reach 56.7 billion dollars, which is the highest ever for that month. These results were driven by the spread of generative AI and the company's focus on advanced memory technology and supplier alliances.

The company will invest 1.4 trillion won over five years to support domestic suppliers of semiconductor materials, parts, and equipment. Trinity Fab, a shared test facility at the Yongin Semiconductor Cluster, will open in May 2027 with a 1,000-pyeong clean room. This 874.6 billion won project includes 55 tools, with SK Hynix contributing 443.2 billion won and the central government adding 373.6 billion won. Local governments will provide 57.7 billion won, while the facility incorporates the specific needs of 217 different materials, components, and equipment suppliers. SK Hynix also plans to invest 600 trillion won to construct four chip fabrication plants at the Yongin semiconductor cluster site.

A company official stated that reaching one trillion dollars in exports resulted from the solidarity of the entire South Korean ecosystem. The official said the company will work with partners to raise competitiveness, drive shared growth, and contribute to national exports. SK Hynix explained that producing top-tier memory requires converging supplier technologies in specialty chemicals, advanced packaging equipment, and precision metrology tools. The company aims to help smaller firms overcome financing and technology challenges through a program covering research, testing, production, and sales. They provide upfront support for early research costs and compensate suppliers even if a project does not meet its targets.

Smaller suppliers are affected because they can now validate new technologies in mass-production environments at a minimum actual maintenance cost. This facility is expected to lower the verification burden for companies that struggle to build their own expensive production equipment. The program also provides 2 trillion won in financing backed by the Korea Trade Insurance Corporation to help these domestic partners. Other support includes the Technology Innovation Company program, a Semiconductor Academy, and youth hiring-linked programs to strengthen the overall workforce. These initiatives aim to bolster the supply chain as competition intensifies within the global market for artificial intelligence chips.

SK Hynix developed the first high-bandwidth memory in 2013 using through-silicon via technology but initially struggled with high costs and demand. The company later applied its proprietary mass reflow-molded underfill process to HBM2E to solve productivity and heat issues for its customers. It expanded its lineup to HBM3, HBM3E, and HBM4, and began supplying samples of a 12-layer HBM4E product this year. In 2024, the firm developed DDR5 using a 10-nanometer-class sixth-generation process and mass-produced 321-layer NAND flash and SOCAMM2 DRAM modules. National semiconductor export shares grew from 15.6 percent in 2023 to 20.8 percent in 2024 and 24.4 percent last year.

The market expects demand for high-bandwidth memory to continue through next year, potentially accelerating the localization of the supply chain. Future export momentum depends on the pace of AI infrastructure investment and changes in the procurement plans of major customers. The technological self-reliance of the supplier ecosystem is another variable that will determine if the current growth trend can be maintained. If Trinity Fab begins operations as scheduled, equipment and materials companies will gain more opportunities for critical mass-production validation. The articles leave open how these variables and the global competition for AI chips will impact long-term semiconductor export figures.
