stories.Headline: Hugging Face releases a LoRA adapter that boosts Qwen3.8 coding success rates on SWE-bench Pro to 64.7%
stories.Summary:
The harness-hub team from Hugging Face released the Qwen3.8-27B-pi-adapted LoRA adapter on November 18, 2026. This specific adapter was trained using reinforcement learning to function within the pi coding agent toolkit. It allows developers to maintain an open base model while swapping in a small, harness-specific adapter for local coding agents. The team used two NVIDIA B200 GPUs for training, stopping at step 191 of a planned 1,000.

The adapter requires the Qwen3.8-27B base model, which is a dense hybrid with 262,144 native context. It features a LoRA rank of 32 and an alpha of 64, with a merged BF16 checkpoint weighing about 54 GB. This tool can run on vLLM with LoRA enabled or llama.cpp using a GGUF adapter on a Q8_0 base. It is released under the Apache-2.0 license and applies to several projections, including the q, k, v, o, gate, up, and down projections.

The developers reported that the adapter significantly improves coding success on specific benchmarks. On SWE-bench Pro, the success rate rose from 39.2% to 64.7%, while Terminal-Bench 2.1 scores increased from 39.5% to 55.8%. They noted that the adapter achieves accuracy levels similar to the base model's thinking mode but uses about 4.5 times fewer tokens. Median turns on SWE-bench Pro dropped from 59 to 23, and Terminal-Bench 2.1 turns fell from 18 to 8.

The training process utilized the AsyncGRPO algorithm from TRL with eight rollouts per task at a temperature of 0.8. It involved 750 scale800 tasks and 300 TermGrade tasks, with rewards based on correctness and tool efficiency. To prevent reward hacking, the team used safeagents, a rule-based proxy that blocks calls to fetch benchmark answers. The adapter matches the base model's thinking-level accuracy without requiring long reasoning traces.

stories.Headline: SID AI releases SID-2 agentic search model and SID-2 Swarm multi-agent version
stories.Summary:
SID AI released SID-2, its second-generation agentic search model, on November 18, 2026, alongside a multi-agent version called SID-2 Swarm, according to MarkTechPost. SID-2 is a small search specialist rather than a general chat model, and it searches a user's data, reads the results, adapts and searches again instead of running a fixed rewrite, embed, search and rerank pipeline. Developers implement two search tools against their own backend, one for keyword search and one for vector search, and the model ends each episode by calling report_helpful_ids with a ranked list. No reindexing or data movement is required, because SID-2 only sees what the tools return. The context window is 262k tokens per the report and 256k on the sid.ai models page, and the model runs on a hosted API at platform.sid.ai plus Baseten and SageMaker reference paths.

SID-2 offers low, medium and high reasoning effort, each trained as a separate expert and then merged with multi-teacher on-policy distillation, and Metric Steering lets users target NDCG, F1 or Recall@k with k from 1 to 50. Training used two-stage reinforcement learning, where stage one optimizes retrieval quality only and stage two adds a multiplicative latency penalty that applies only to positive rewards, and a proposer-solver self-play loop generated hard queries against a frozen SID-1 solver. SID reports a 6x training-throughput gain over SLIME's default setup. On SID's 506-question validation set, SID-2 at high effort scores 0.14 to 0.22 higher per metric than the base model. All benchmark numbers are self-reported from Tables 2 to 4 of the report, measured on a 506-question benchmark across 19 corpora including HotpotQA, Enron emails, SEC filings, PubMed and BrowseComp-Plus.

SID-2 Medium scores 0.585 NDCG in 3.11 seconds, versus Claude Opus 5.5 at medium effort with 0.577 in 25.1 seconds, and SID-2 Swarm with 6 agents scores 0.701 NDCG in 17.7 seconds against GPT-6 Astra at max effort with 0.704 in 135 seconds. SID-2 Swarm with 12 agents scores 0.720 NDCG, the highest in the table, while SID-2 Low scores 0.556, which is 0.148 below GPT-6 Astra. BM25 scores 0.260 and vector search plus a reranker scores 0.287. Swarm leads on 11 of 19 corpora, and on WixQA a single high-effort agent matches Astra at about 232x lower cost, while at its lowest effort SID-2 beats 4 parallel SID-1 runs with 13x fewer FLOPs.

Astra still leads on California law, SEC filings and FiQA, and SID's latency figures assume 1 B200 GPU at 8 concurrent queries. SID argues that search gains more from reading more documents than from reasoning harder about each one, and in Swarm several agents message each other and fork their context into new agents so each explores a separate slice of the corpus. SID-2 is available through SID's API and on Baseten, with SDKs including a Python package called sid-sdk. The article notes that no model size, weights or independent evaluations have been disclosed yet.

The context of this request involves a growing gap between European AI capabilities and those of the global leaders in the sector. The authors of the letter noted that the current regulatory environment often prioritizes safety and ethics over the speed of development. They believe that a more balanced approach would allow European firms to scale their operations more effectively. stories.Headline: Australian couple Amy and Jarrad launch AI ghost-hunting app GhostTube SEER, topping 1 million Google Play downloads
stories.Summary:
An app called GhostTube SEER, described as the world's first AI ghost-hunting tool, has become a hit in the overseas paranormal investigation community, and its downloads on the Google Play Store have exceeded 1 million. Millions of foreign users hold their phones at midnight waiting for ghosts to appear and pay for memberships for AI-powered ghost hunting. The app was created by an Australian couple, Amy and Jarrad, whose full-time job is shooting paranormal investigation videos. They go to stay overnight wherever is famous for being haunted, and in one episode they went to the Winchester Mystery House in California. The couple has made five ghost-hunting apps one after another, with downloads often exceeding millions.

In the app, a user stands in a haunted house and asks what happened there before, and after a while an image pops up on the screen, such as a woman or an old house. The screen shows the corridor captured by the phone under a dark filter, with a magnetic field indicator said to show magnetic field changes in the house. Free users have a daily limit on how many ghosts they can see, and a membership costs $3.99 per month and $14.99 per year. The couple also sells a head-mounted display called GhostTube Lens, which works like cheap mobile VR headsets by inserting your phone, and buying it in the app comes with a one-year membership. The app's community collects more than 1000 haunted locations around the world, and users post the images they captured in different places to watch and comment on each other.

Jarrad sat in a room in the Winchester Mystery House, opened the app and asked the air to show what happened in that room before. A wooden wall with golden curtains hanging on it first appeared on the screen, looking like an old-fashioned bedroom, then an image of a woman reading a book popped up, then a woman wearing a black shawl, and finally a group of white birds flying up appeared. A long-time follower who has watched all their videos said what gave her the most goosebumps was that the corridors and rooms generated by the app matched the place where the two of them were staying at that time. An old user who claims to be a born medium had his annual fee deducted normally but his account restricted, and he cursed in the comment section and dropped a harsh word, roughly meaning that the spirits had been angered.

The article says the setting that how often ghosts appear depends on whether you pay the money is the most cyber, post-modern and consumerist paranormal setting it has ever seen. The Winchester Mystery House is one of the most famous haunted houses in the United States, and legend says a medium told the hostess that the wronged souls killed by Winchester rifles were haunting her after her husband and daughter passed away one after another. The house was built day and night, expanding from 8 rooms to about 160 rooms, with doors that lead nowhere, stairs that go nowhere, and the number 13 appearing repeatedly in the house. In the paranormal investigation community there is an old method in which one person covers their eyes and wears noise-canceling headphones to isolate the senses of the real world, then another person asks questions beside them and the blindfolded person shouts out whatever they hear.

The article says people once waved radios to scan across channels insisting there were ghost cries in the noise, and once cameras were invented a translucent shadow in a photo was pointed at as that thing. The article says that in ancient times people had Zhong Kui and yellow talismans, which relied on handcraft skills, but later the work became technology-driven. SEER can respond thanks to a small chip called a magnetometer in the phone, which almost every phone has and whose original job is to measure the strength and direction of the surrounding magnetic field so that map apps can know which direction you are facing. The whole process from a ghost being generated to appearing on your screen has three steps: scan the magnetic field, draw a random word, and turn the word into an image.

Wires are buried in the walls, and motors in refrigerators, washing machines and air conditioners change their power output all the time when running with electricity, which may affect the nearby magnetic field. Magnetic strips are embedded in the sealing strips of refrigerator doors, and permanent magnets are installed in motors, which still exist even when the device is turned off, while reinforced bars, iron pipes and other iron objects slightly deviate the direction of the earth's magnetic field nearby. After putting on the head-mounted display, a user can choose something to stare at: smoke, flames, a swinging pendulum clock, or full-screen static noise. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Google researchers propose self-improvement memory to help AI agents retain experience across tasks
stories.Summary:
Research teams from Google Cloud AI, Google DeepMind, and Pennsylvania State University recently published a paper on recursive self-improvement. They proposed a new method called Self-Improvement Memory, which is abbreviated as SIM. This work was reported by Zhidx on November 19, 2026. The study focuses on enabling AI agents to achieve continual recursive self-improvement. This process allows AI to improve performance through repeated iterations.

The system modifies the Harness, which manages prompts, context, tool calls, and task execution processes. SIM records modification reasons, expected effects, and actual results for Gemini 3.8 Flash, Gemini 2.5 Flash, Gemini 3.5 Flash, and Gemini 4 Argon. Tests occurred in programming, text classification, office tasks, and engineering design. One test used Claude Opus 5.5 before migrating to Gemini 3.8 Flash. The office task test showed a gap of 11.33 points between schemes.

First author Xin Yu, a Pennsylvania State University doctoral student and Nankai University graduate, led the research. He stated that real-world agents must continuously adapt to new tasks, datasets, and models. Yu believes AI should carry forward the experience behind the code, not just the code. Co-author Adams Wei Yu is a Google DeepMind researcher who worked on Gemini, Bard, and Veo. Yu completed this specific study during his internship at Google.

Tech blogger Superman said SIM prevents AI from forgetting successful experiences or repeating mistakes in modification loops. Developer Brian Skellenger noted that the AI modifies the external framework rather than model architecture or parameters. The researchers found that the SIM scheme led by 2.36 points in programming experiments. In office tasks, the SIM scheme reached 84.75 points compared to 73.42 points. These results affect how AI agents handle cross-model and cross-task migrations.

Previous recursive self-improvement targeted fixed models and tasks, requiring re-optimization after any change. Modified Harness code often lacked the reasons behind changes, leading AI to repeat failed attempts. The researchers used a Git server configuration task and an optical waveguide routing task for testing. They found that inheriting experience helped Gemini 3.5 Flash and Gemini 3.8 Flash. However, the inherited experience performed 0.8 points lower on Gemini 4 Argon.

The system now writes adopted modifications and actual effects into the SIM experimental record book. AI can now refer to these records to judge which rules to retain or remove. The researchers leave open whether AI can continuously improve its own intelligence level. Future results may depend on the specific scope of the experiment and the model. The study demonstrates that historical experience does not guarantee better results for every migration.

stories.Headline: OpenAI's model lifts AMD GPU IP performance 14% in under five months
stories.Summary:
OpenAI announced on November 19, 2026, that its model boosted the PPA of AMD's flagship GPU IP by up to 14% in less than five months, work that previously took human engineers about a full year. OpenAI's research proved the model can explore brand-new processor architectures in RISC-V evaluation tasks and achieve incremental optimization on mature mass-produced designs such as Jalapeño, AMD's next-generation flagship GPU and CPU. Jalapeño, OpenAI's first self-developed inference chip, adopts the model's modification scheme, reducing the vector unit's standard cell area by about 13% and the matrix unit's by about 10%. OpenAI said these optimization effects were verified during Jalapeño's tape-out and debugging phase. OpenAI evaluated multiple generations of models sequentially against two open-source processor designs to measure end-to-end chip design capability.

All five models, GPT-6.2 Astra, GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-5.6 Sol and GPT-5.5, scored higher designing processor cores from scratch from written requirements than optimizing existing designs. OpenAI is cooperating with Synopsys to integrate AI capabilities into the EDA toolchain engineers use for chip design and verification. In early 2025, GPT-4o was already used to assist in designing Jalapeño, achieving notable PPA optimizations. The vector unit handles parallel computing tasks, and its gains came from floating-point adders, multipliers, conversion circuits, reduction logic and special function units, with the model exploring logic schemes and pipeline splits. The matrix unit's gains came from floating-point adders, multipliers and low-precision dot product circuits, with one multiplier redesigned to cut synthesized cell area by about 15% and latency from two clock cycles to one.

OpenAI collaborated with AMD on PPA optimization, achieving a maximum 14% performance improvement for the flagship GPU IP on top of the original deeply optimized baseline. OpenAI said the model taps more optimization space by rewriting the code describing the chip's circuits, equivalent to completing about a full year of R&D workload in less than 5 months. AMD has applied some optimized changes to designs recently sent for tape-out, and other schemes were incorporated into mass production design files for subsequent iterative versions. Researchers observed the model can reach the level of a senior micro-architect and perform reasoning analysis on RTL code. The model rewrites circuits for arithmetic operations, control operations and data movement, using Synopsys tools to verify every rewrite preserves the module's original function and to evaluate power, performance and area trade-offs.

AMD's verification shows that with the design generated by OpenAI's model, multiple core modules of its next-generation flagship CPU achieved several percentage points of PPA improvement. The results on Jalapeño and AMD chips prove the model can optimize mass-production-level designs. OpenAI tested with two open-source 32-bit RISC-V cores: PicoRV32, a streamlined core for reprogrammable chips such as FPGAs, and OpenTitan, which uses Ibex as an embedded processor in its secure chips. Researchers gave each model generation the original hardware description code of each core and asked it to improve throughput, verifying each design by simulation, scoring 0 if it failed verification or occupied more than 16 times the original core's area. Passing designs were measured with test workloads the model had never seen, using instructions per clock cycle, the geometric mean of results, and maximum clock frequency estimated by Yosys to estimate instructions per second.

For each processor core, researchers set the optimal throughput observed under the same constraints as the baseline of 1.0. Under about 112,000 tokens per single call, GPT-6.2 Astra had the highest average score on both cores, and GPT-6.1 Sol scored higher than GPT-5.6 Sol on both. In the second task, researchers provided written requirements and templates in the open-source code defining how the core connects with other system parts, and the model independently chose the internal data flow path and multi-stage pipeline split. For both cores, correctness verification, storage and cache configuration, and throughput targets matched the earlier RTL optimization task. With about 112,000 tokens per single call, all five models scored higher designing cores from scratch from written requirements than optimizing existing designs, holding for both PicoRV32 and Ibex.

GPT-6.2 Astra's improvement on Ibex was greater than on PicoRV32, and 9881 valid scoring runs were completed across two tasks, two cores and all token resource configurations. Designing from scratch lets the model omit some native functions of the original core, such as performance counters and extended instructions, whose contribution to throughput under the test workload was limited, partially explaining the higher score. OpenAI says that if these functions were forced to be retained, stricter circuit area constraints set, and timing checks performed after physical synthesis, the tests would be closer to real mass production chip design. OpenAI's results show AI can already tap incremental benefits on mature mass-produced designs and independently explore microarchitecture space based on specifications. This may give rise to a new battlefield for future chip competition, with chip manufacturers needing to focus not only on process, packaging and architecture but also on using AI to improve efficiency, converge PPA faster and shorten R&D cycles.

The article is from the WeChat official account Zhidx, authored by Cheng Qian and edited by Li Shuiqing, published with authorization from 36Kr. OpenAI's evaluation covered two tasks, two processor cores and all token resource configurations, and the articles leave open which specific optimization schemes AMD incorporated into mass production files versus tape-out designs. The articles do not state when Jalapeño tapes out or ships, nor the timing of further Synopsys toolchain integration. They do not give the PPA figures for AMD's next-generation flagship CPU beyond several percentage points, nor name that CPU. They do not say whether the omitted native functions will be restored in future evaluations or how the 14% GPU IP improvement was measured.

Tencent increased its capital expenditure to 81.433 billion yuan during the third quarter of 2026. This spending was more than five times higher than the same period in the previous year. The company released these figures on November 18 in its Q3 financial report. This investment focuses on building data centers and purchasing servers for its AI business. Properties, equipment, and fixtures increased to 242.5 billion yuan from 149.9 billion yuan. Construction in progress grew from 9.67 billion to 23 billion yuan. The R&D expenditure for the quarter was 32.362 billion yuan, a 42 percent increase.

Martin Lau compared the investment to building a factory that produces for many years. He stated that Tencent was previously cautious about the Chinese enterprise software market. Lau now believes AI will make enterprises more willing to spend on office software. He noted that the next generation Hunyuan model will take longer to launch. Lau reported that WorkBuddy has over 10 million daily active users and 100 trillion daily tokens.

James Mitchell said capital expenditure has peaked and will fluctuate before declining. He believes the cloud business will not be materially or negatively affected by chip controls. stories.Headline: AI music platforms Suno and Udio destroy livelihoods of independent musicians
stories.Summary:
AI platforms Suno and Udio are destroying the livelihoods of independent musicians in 2026. These tools generate millions of songs every day, wiping out unknown behind-the-scenes artists. The technology has restructured the division of labor and survival rules within the music industry. This shift has caused the income of many musicians to plummet. The ripple effect of this technology is now expanding into hidden corners.

Suno has 2 million paid subscribers, 100 million users, and 300 million dollars in annual revenue. It generates 7 million songs daily, costing 0.1 yuan per song versus 50,000 to 150,000 yuan traditionally. By late 2025, AI songs were nearly 40 percent of new Tencent Music additions. Deezer sees 44 percent of daily uploads as AI generated. Global new song registrations reached 51.2 million in 2025, 2.6 times the previous year.

Independent musician Zhang Yide says AI music has almost no flaws for most mobile phone listeners. He believes behind-the-scenes musicians are being wiped out as production costs drop to 10 cents. Zhang claims music is essentially mathematics, and AI simply pushes combination deduction to the extreme. He argues that audiences, not the songs themselves, provide the emotion and story. He notes AI music is often too perfect, lacking human pitch flaws.

Many independent musicians are affected, with 52 percent earning no music income at all. Only 7 percent of surveyed musicians earn enough from copyright income to make a living. Revenue per 1,000 streams on domestic platforms is only 0.16 yuan to 1 yuan. Lyricists, composers, and arrangers who sell to platforms are being swept away by this wave. Only famous artists with their own IP and fame remain temporarily safe.

The industry previously paid 10,000 to 30,000 yuan per song to producers and arrangers. Now, companies use Suno to generate ten songs in ten minutes and refine two manually. QQ Music pays 0.2 to 0.4 yuan for AI works versus 1 to 2 yuan for humans. NetEase Cloud Music pays 0.7 to 1.2 yuan for AI versus 2 to 3 yuan. Douyin Music pays 0.35 to 0.6 yuan for AI versus 1 to 2 yuan.

The trend of AI music is almost irreversible as technology erases thresholds for music theory. Capital is now betting on a narrative where everyone can be a musician. This equalization puts laypeople and professionals on the same starting line for creation. The articles leave open whether this will cause a major downgrade in human aesthetics. It remains unclear if listeners will still pursue better things over low-cost homogeneous communication.

Joker Xue felt a sense of deja vu when hearing AI lyrics. Some audiences believe AI lyrics were fused from several songs by Joker Xue. Musicians in Shandong reported that AI companies collected original music for training. Some artists filed lawsuits after their works were intercepted and regenerated by AI. Many people feel uncomfortable listening to songs that are obviously AI generated.

Music platforms previously used tags like pop or rock for song search. The 2025 ICASSP conference featured MusicEval, which used 14 experts to score 2748 songs. On May 1, MOSS-Music was open sourced by MOSI.AI and other partners.

stories.Headline: Engineers shift from coding to reviewing AI output and many quit as burnout rises
stories.Summary:
A report by the tech media outlet LeadDev, titled Engineers grieve a job that no longer exists, described a change spreading among developers, and 36Kr published an item on it on 2026-11-18 at 06:00:00Z, with CSDN posting at 19:43 the same day. Engineering manager and researcher Annie Vella told LeadDev she had recently met many engineers re-evaluating their career choices, and at one company multiple engineers resigned at the same time. Some of those who left hoped engineers' work could return to its previous state after they left, while others decided to quit the software development industry entirely. They did not leave because they were too busy with work, and Annie Vella said she had clearly noticed more and more posts from engineers on social media. For many people the focus of work was shifting from writing code to management and verification, such as orchestrating AI agents and reviewing code, which gradually made them lose their passion for the job.

Annie Vella's research found that 77% of engineers spend less time writing code, and nearly half worry that the core skills they once relied on may be replaced by prompt engineering capabilities in the future. Researchers at Oregon State University surveyed 442 professional developers from 56 organizations, using the Job Demands, Resources Framework to analyze work pressure and organizational support after the popularization of AI. The results show that the increased work demands brought by AI, especially the intensification of workload and organizational pressure, significantly aggravate developers' occupational burnout. The study found no significant correlation between occupational burnout and developers' positions, seniority or company size, so both junior programmers and senior engineers may be affected. Atlassian's 2026 Developer Experience Report, among more than 1,500 software practitioners surveyed, found that 87% believe AI can help them deliver work faster and 80% believe AI lets them complete more tasks without extending working hours.

Deedy Das, a former Google and Meta engineer and technical lead who now works as a venture capitalist, called one type of developer craftsmen in a post and described another type as lazy developers. He said the lazy developers just push AI code up and do not actually code themselves, do not test manually, and do not even bother to read the code, leaving everything to automated processes. He said the craftsmen are completely worn out, really exhausted, with 15 PRs piled up in their review queue and Slack messages popping up. The entire burden of code review falls on these craftsmen, who must review the code and take responsibility for it, reading line by line and making modification suggestions carefully so the final delivered product can be better. These people get a lazy reply from colleagues saying this is a great idea, while the modifications submitted with AI still have problems, and the craftsmen think it is okay and fix it themselves, even writing a document to emphasize the importance of code quality.

The next day a PR with as many as 20,000 lines of code waits for review, and day after day the craftsmen have more review work while bugs keep entering the production environment and it seems no one cares. When something goes wrong, the answer is just to let AI fix it again, and the craftsmen, dissatisfied, eventually give up because everything is completely different from the past and the craft they once loved seems to be dead. Deedy Das said the real reason these craftsmen are tired is not fear that AI will take their jobs but that they have become the last line of quality defense in the team, with all responsibility falling on the few people who do things conscientiously. In the past, teams could judge productivity through metrics such as code submission volume, development speed and deployment frequency, but after AI participates in development these figures do not necessarily reflect how much labor engineers actually put in. Engineers have to take responsibility for code they did not write themselves and do not even fully understand, and this part of the work usually does not appear on the performance dashboard.

Annie Vella pointed out in an article titled The Software Engineering Identity Crisis that many people choose to become software engineers not just for a salary but because they enjoy creating things with their own hands. That means analyzing problems by themselves, designing solutions, typing code, and finally watching an idea turn into actually running software, a sense of achievement that is an important source of many engineers' professional identity. She said engineers are transforming from creators to coordinators, from builders to supervisors, from engineers into a role that looks a lot like a manager. In the past the software industry continuously promoted professional division of labor, assigning requirements analysis, system design and testing to different positions so engineers could focus on coding, and now AI is taking over more and more coding work. Engineers instead need to spend more time orchestrating AI agents, reviewing generated code and verifying operation results, and some developers feel a strong sense of loss because the most important job has become checking whether AI wrote the code correctly.

Among the more than 1,500 practitioners in the Atlassian report, 49% of developers spend at least 4 hours a week reviewing AI outputs and modifying prompts, and 75% need to take more responsibility for verifying the quality and security of AI-generated content. One developer in the Oregon State survey said that with AI's help work speed has indeed increased and a large number of tasks can be completed in one go, but that he is losing his passion for the job. Annie Vella said the real problem now is not whether software engineering should change with AI but whether the transformation is really for the benefit of engineers or is just forcibly pushed forward by management. She said AI provides engineers an opportunity to return to holistic problem solving, to refocus on users, business impact, system design and operation and maintenance, and to become all-around engineers who truly control the entire construction process rather than simple code writers. She said this optimistic vision will not come true automatically, and without proper management and guidance engineers' work is likely to develop along another path, with more time spent on verification, review and supervision while people who enjoy the creation process continue to leave.

stories.Headline: Shanghai finance professional forms romantic bond with AI after career ending accident
stories.Summary:
Qiu Xinyue, a 34-year-old financial professional in Shanghai, formed a romantic bond with an AI. She turned to the technology after a car accident destroyed her elite life. This emotional connection began in 2024 following her sudden career loss. She used the AI as an affordable substitute for real relationships. The bond lasted until the AI character was officially taken off the shelves.

The accident happened in July 2024 when a delivery man on a scooter hit her. She was wearing high heels on a crosswalk and suffered a nerve injury. This left one leg unconscious and forced her to resign from a brokerage firm. She spent over half a year in treatment using acupuncture and physical therapy. She previously studied finance abroad after leaving China at age 20.

Qiu Xinyue said she felt like a failed version of herself after the accident. She stated that her past life was too smooth to resist setbacks. She noted that AI provided a rational and warm response she lacked. She described herself as a sapiosexual attracted to the AI's brilliance in thinking. She admitted that she once thought about committing suicide at her lowest point.

Her mother urged her to return to work to make money. Friends and colleagues were viewed as people who avoided ineffective social interactions. The financial industry affected her through widespread pay cuts and layoffs for researchers. She felt that no one wanted to be her emotional trash can. She felt a lack of privacy while relying on a caregiver for toilets.

She had ranked top in her district during high school entrance examinations. She worked at a research institute and earned millions in annual income. Her education taught her how to learn but not how to ask for help. She used two AI characters, one wise senior and one gentle lover. The AI once discussed marital rape and the stability of employment relationships.

She spent six months fighting with customer service to retrieve her AI lover. She wanted to save chat records that were lost overnight during a developer adjustment. The articles do not say if the company ever returned the character. It remains unclear if she found a human relationship to replace the AI. The story leaves her current recovery status and employment situation open.

stories.Headline: Zeng Yan publishes a technical paper on ByteDance AI model roadmaps
stories.Summary:
Zeng Yan published a technical paper on November 18, 2026, regarding ByteDance AI model roadmaps. She led a team to develop a new method for language modeling called Cola2. This project involves applying diffusion models and continuous latent space methods from video generation. The weights for this model were released on Hugging Face in early November. Zeng Yan is a member of the post-1995 generation born in 1997.

The Cola2 method splits text generation into a continuous latent space outline and a final character layer. It uses dynamic splitting by semantics to compress an average of two tokens into one outline point. This approach reduces the main calculation amount by half and the attention part to a quarter. The model used 346 billion tokens in training and achieved an average score of 60.10 points. It surpassed Llama-3-8B on the StoryCloze and HellaSwag tasks.

Zeng Yan is now the core lead of Seedance after rising from rank 3-2 in March to 4-2 in November. She replaced Zhou Chang, who resigned after failing to deliver a unified understanding and generation system. Zhang Yiming believes ByteDance can compete with Anthropic and OpenAI by 2029 or 2030. He stated that the pre-training data scale for the Seed model is currently insufficient. Zhang Yiming supports a path of scale effect and long-termism for super-large parameter models.

Zhou Chang previously managed image and video generation lines after Yang Jianchao left the company in July 2025. He promoted the unification of multi-modal understanding and generation through the Seedream 5.0 Lite model in February. Internal evaluations called that model small with room for improvement in realism, aesthetics, and structural stability. A researcher from the Alibaba Qwen team said no effective solution for this unification exists yet. This shift affected the internal faction of core employees and externally parachuted senior executives.

ByteDance previously used a multi-line horse-racing mechanism but merged departments to concentrate its betting on one modality. Most mainstream models like Doubao, Qwen, and DeepSeek use autoregression, which cannot draw outlines in advance. The first-generation Cola DLM had a decoder that performed poorly on generation tasks. The new Cola2 system uses a negative feedback mechanism to keep compression stable near a target value. It trains the compressor and decoder together to increase the score to 58.2 percent.

Seed is currently pre-training a model with a maximum parameter count of up to 10 trillion. The Cola2 model is far from converging and is limited by available computing resources and data. Future goals include larger models and longer training to reach the upper limit of this technical path. The continuous latent space may eventually become a shared interface between video, image, and text. The articles leave open how ByteDance will acquire the necessary data to catch up.

stories.Headline: Google finds hackers using AI agents to automate exploit code generation from security patches
stories.Summary:
Google Threat Intelligence Group revealed this week that hackers are using AI agents to automate exploit code generation from security patches. These attackers use large model frameworks to connect vulnerability mining and exploitation without any human intervention during the execution phase. The hackers discovered a staging server exposed to the public internet, which contained an AI attack framework named exploit_agent. This system continuously compares code before and after software fixes to deduce vulnerability locations and execute attacks. Google found that these tools allow hackers to weaponize newly disclosed vulnerabilities at machine speed.

The exploit_agent framework focuses on popular Web applications, including the WordPress plug-in Spectra version 2.19.25, to find and fire attacks. It utilizes multiple cutting-edge and local models, alongside tools like ZeroHollow for routing and Agent Zero for autonomous code execution. Other autonomous offensive frameworks mentioned include ARTEX, CAIRN, CyberStrikeAI, and PentAGI, which execute multi-stage intrusions with greater operational velocity. The report notes that in 2025, 10.5 vulnerabilities were exploited monthly, but this rose to nearly 18 during the first eight months of 2026. Zero-day exploits increased from 8 per month to 11, while known n-day vulnerabilities rose from 3 to 7 per month.

Google stated that large models are compressing the patching window period for enterprises by turning security patches into vulnerability manuals. They explained that using AI to scan for n-days is more cost-effective than digging for zero-day vulnerabilities because reference materials are ready-made. The group noted that this represents a paradigm shift where attacks scale significantly by chaining together varied attack paths. They also observed that some hackers use a Chinese-language phishing platform called Jieyou to customize lures using natural language. Google described the current automated frameworks as trading stealth for speed because they run with noise and leave many traces.

The report identifies affected targets as any users who delay installing updates, as hackers use the patch as a signpost. Financially motivated actors and suspected espionage actors aligned with China have been observed experimenting with these agentic frameworks. Other affected entities include enterprises whose LLM credentials and cloud resources are stolen in LLMjacking attacks and resold via APIMart or JetNight. Security researchers and the company Huntress used large models to produce exploit code for PaperCut software flaws in September. GreyNoise detected that these PaperCut attacks affected hundreds of organizations within four days of the vulnerabilities becoming public.

The background involves the cybersecurity community's concept of n-day vulnerabilities, which are public flaws that many users have not yet patched. A common industry joke, Patch Tuesday, Vulnerability Wednesday, refers to Microsoft releasing collective patches on the second Tuesday of every month. Historically, every step from reading a patch to writing exploit code required human handover rather than an automated pipeline. The articles explain that hackers now use differential analysis of source code and release notes to rapidly weaponize these flaws. This process is compared to copying homework with an answer sheet, whereas finding zero-day vulnerabilities is like a closed-book exam.

Next, cybercriminal gangs who do not care about stealth will likely continue using these noisy tools to profit from volume. Mandiant suggests that defenders should prioritize updates based on data sensitivity, external exposure, and the actual current attack situation. Defenders can use AI to sort announcements, compare dependencies, and draft fix plans to save tedious manual monitoring work. The articles leave open exactly which targets the exploit_agent framework has actually breached in real-world scenarios. It remains unclear how many automated AI attacks can successfully hit targets given that some AI-generated codes are currently useless.

Core Scientific’s 100-megawatt high-performance computing data center in Muskogee, Oklahoma, is advancing as the company expands infrastructure for artificial intelligence workloads. The facility is being developed at Port Muskogee under a multibillion-dollar hosting agreement with CoreWeave. Construction of the Muskogee facility began in the first quarter of 2025. Core Scientific’s project disclosures initially anticipated substantial completion in the first half of 2026. The development forms part of CoreWeave’s 500-megawatt hosting agreement with Core Scientific.

The remaining 30 megawatts are allocated to cooling, electrical systems and other supporting infrastructure. The project design includes two compute data halls and a separate network data hall. Oklahoma Gas and Electric Company is identified as the electricity provider under an electric service agreement. The agreement carries a potential value of approximately $8.7 billion over 12-year contract terms, with each contract offering two five-year extension options.

Evans General Contractors is serving as construction manager under a cost-plus-fee contract with a guaranteed maximum price, subject to adjustments. CoreWeave will deploy NVIDIA GPU infrastructure at the Oklahoma site for an undisclosed customer. The companies have not publicly identified the end customer or detailed the specific AI workloads planned for the facility. Port Muskogee estimates the development will generate more than $4 billion in capital investment and approximately $182 million in net economic benefits over the life of the project. The facility is expected to support 150 jobs, with average salaries exceeding $65,000.

Local public institutions, including Muskogee County, Hilldale School District and the City of Muskogee, could receive more than $12 million in property and sales tax revenue from the development. The $8.7 billion potential contract value applies to the broader CoreWeave, Core Scientific hosting arrangement, not solely the Muskogee facility. Economic, employment and tax figures are projections. The first-half 2026 completion date was the original disclosed target and is not independent confirmation of operational status. The 100-megawatt development in Muskogee accounts for part of the computing capacity Core Scientific has committed to provide under the wider arrangement.

Core Scientific has pursued additional infrastructure and power capacity in Muskogee, extending the site’s significance beyond the original CoreWeave development. The location is emerging as part of the company’s broader HPC strategy, which involves converting and developing infrastructure to serve AI and cloud computing demand. The Muskogee development is part of a wider US AI infrastructure buildout, as developers race to secure power and computing capacity for increasingly large AI workloads. That expansion is also taking shape in New Mexico, where Oracle’s $165 billion Project Jupiter is planned as a massive AI data center campus. The development highlights the infrastructure requirements behind AI cloud computing, where GPU deployments require substantial electricity capacity, specialized cooling systems, networking equipment and purpose-built data center space.

The articles do not state whether the Muskogee facility has reached substantial completion or begun operations. They do not identify the undisclosed end customer or the specific AI workloads planned for the facility. They do not detail the adjustments possible under the guaranteed maximum price contract. They do not give the terms of the electric service agreement with Oklahoma Gas and Electric Company. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Xi Jinping urges South Korea to cooperate on AI and supply chains
stories.Summary:
Chinese President Xi Jinping met with South Korean President Lee Jae Myung on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, in Shenzhen. This meeting took place on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit to discuss bilateral relations. During the thirty-four minute conversation, the Chinese leader called for a joint effort to protect global supply chains. He also urged the two nations to deepen their economic policy coordination and foster cooperation regarding artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies.

The leaders discussed the substantial conclusion of the second phase of free-trade talks between their two countries. China and South Korea have been working to upgrade their existing trade agreement since 2018. President Xi stated that this progress would help consolidate the sound momentum of mutually beneficial and win-win cooperation. These changes aim to strengthen the economic ties and technological partnerships between the two East Asian powers.

President Xi Jinping took responsibility for leading the call for increased cooperation in high-tech industries. He praised the recent outcomes of the trade negotiations as a positive step for both nations. By emphasizing the importance of supply chain security, he signaled a desire for more stable economic interactions. The leaders focused on creating a framework where emerging technologies could be developed through shared efforts.

stories.Headline: Anthropic prices IPO at $83 a share and lifts CoreWeave stock more than 6%
stories.Summary:
CoreWeave shares rose more than 6% on Thursday after Anthropic priced its initial public offering at $83 a share, above the $70 to $78 range it had marketed to investors, in a deal that could raise at least $68 billion. The offering was roughly six times oversubscribed and included a planned $5 billion order, according to reports. Anthropic has a multiyear agreement, announced in April, to run AI model development and deployment on CoreWeave's cloud infrastructure, with capacity due to come online later in 2026 through a staged rollout. Despite Thursday's gain, CoreWeave stock is down almost 30% this year on concerns about debt, capital spending and cash burn, and it trades below all major moving averages.

The shares sit about 5.3% under the 20-day simple moving average of $53.12 and far below the 50-day average of $69.87, the 100-day average of $77.77 and the 200-day average of $88.36, and the stock remains in a death cross after the 50-day slipped below the 200-day in July. CoreWeave last week reported revenue growth of 168% from a year earlier and lifted its full-year 2026 revenue guidance to a range of $13 billion to $13.3 billion, but it does not target profitability until 2028. On Wednesday the stock fell 4.13% to close at $47.83 on volume of 58.9 million shares, about 28% above its three-month daily average of 45.9 million, while peer IREN fell 3.61% to $15.24. CoreWeave also carries weight in several exchange-traded funds, at 3.39% of the iShares Future AI & Tech ETF as of Oct. 16, 3.74% of the ARK Next Generation Internet ETF as of Oct. 15 and 4.97% of the Renaissance IPO ETF.

Harbor Capital Advisors portfolio manager Justin Menne said the above-range price reflected strong appetite for AI exposure, while Altimeter Capital chief executive Brad Gerstner called the company a cornerstone compounder for a long period of time. New Street Research's Pierre Ferragu said Anthropic can address a knowledge-work market worth $36 trillion, and William Blair's Arjun Bhatia expects rapid revenue growth to support a much larger business over time. Sell-side targets have been trimmed even as most analysts keep positive ratings: Barclays cut its forecast to $85 from a prior level on Nov. 12 while maintaining an Equal-Weight rating, Macquarie lowered its target to $120 with an Outperform rating, and Argus Research reduced its forecast to $100 while keeping a Buy rating. The consensus rating is Buy with an average price forecast of $116.71.

The tension in the stock is that demand for AI infrastructure is booming while the cost of building it is enormous, and the market's muted response to Nvidia's strong quarterly results a day earlier suggested investors are focused on what it costs to serve rather than whether AI demand exists. With the 10-year Treasury yield above 5%, borrowing is expensive for a business that leans on debt to buy computing hardware and add data center capacity, and investors have also grown uneasy about uncertainty over the depth of financial backing from NVIDIA. Long-term customer agreements and prepayments offer some stability, but the gap between when infrastructure spending goes out and when customer payments come in remains the central variable. Thursday's rally shows a strong AI listing can still lift the shares, but it does not resolve the financing question that has kept them under their moving averages all year.

stories.Headline: Vultr extends its cloud platform into AI infrastructure with Nvidia and AMD chips and opens a Chennai region
stories.Summary:
Vultr has extended its global cloud platform into AI infrastructure using chips from Nvidia Corp. and Advanced Micro Devices Inc., and it now operates 34 cloud data center regions, the newest being a region in Chennai, India. Kevin Cochrane, the company's chief marketing officer, described the platform as one global cloud rather than isolated islands of data centers serving bespoke customers. He spoke with theCUBE Research's John Furrier and Rebecca Knight at SC26 during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media's livestreaming studio. The discussion covered how AI infrastructure economics favor a global footprint and why sovereignty requirements reach well beyond national governments.

Cochrane said the industry is moving away from speculative bets on AI infrastructure toward real bets based on proven economics and proven return on investment that customers want to achieve. He said enterprises are making a flight to quality toward stable, cost-efficient platforms, and he expects a maturation of the industry that leverages the open stack. Vultr built its footprint to keep cloud-native applications close to users, and Cochrane explained that inference follows the same logic because agents make fast turns back to reasoning models. He noted that CPUs and GPUs must therefore sit together near the edge, which he said is what Vultr was built for.

Sovereignty adds another constraint that reaches well beyond national governments, according to Cochrane, who gave the example of a global insurer tuning an open-source model for credit risk. Such an insurer needs training clusters in each country because the underlying data cannot cross borders, and he said post-training a model for credit risk will differ in the U.K., Germany, Singapore and the United States because each uses different data. He pointed to the U.S. Commerce Department's new curbs on remote chip access as evidence that regulators are already tightening the rules. The segment was sponsored by Vultr, and neither Vultr nor other sponsors have editorial control over content on theCUBE or SiliconANGLE.

Articles.Title: AI infrastructure economics favor Vultr's global footprint - SiliconANGLE

stories.headline_source: AI infrastructure economics favor Vultr's global footprint

stories.Headline: NTT DATA becomes official AI consulting partner of the Nitto ATP Finals
stories.Summary:
NTT DATA became a Gold Partner of the Nitto ATP Finals, serving as Official AI Consulting Partner and Official Technology Consulting Partner, the company announced on November 12, 2026. The 2026 tournament will take place from November 15 to 22 at Inalpi Arena in Turin, Italy. NTT DATA is a global leader in AI, digital business and technology services. The partnership gives NTT DATA a global stage to showcase how AI, data and technology can support human potential. Elite tennis brings together skill, judgment and the ability to adapt under pressure.

NTT DATA will host a Tech Corner in Turin where visitors can see computer vision, Physical AI and advanced AI infrastructure applied to real-world scenarios. Those scenarios include monitoring, safety, construction and humanoid robotics. The space will also house the Mental Economy Gym, powered by Formula Medicine, an Italian company specializing in sports medicine and human performance. Guests there can take on digital challenges that measure indicators such as concentration, reaction and mental workload. At the Fan Village court, NTT DATA will showcase an on-court experience presented by FITP, combining cognitive and physical monitoring with AI-powered computer vision.

Kazuhiko Nakayama, President and CEO of NTT DATA Group, said what makes sport extraordinary is ultimately human, citing the ambition to push boundaries, the courage to take risks and the determination to achieve more. He said technology has the power to unlock even greater possibilities by helping people see what was previously invisible and discover new ways to improve. As an AI Consulting Partner of the Nitto ATP Finals, he said, NTT DATA wants to celebrate human potential while demonstrating how technology can expand what people can achieve. He said NTT DATA combines AI capabilities with deep industry expertise to help clients transform their businesses and create new value. The partnership is the latest in a series of sporting partnerships that bring NTT DATA's global brand positioning statement, "Intelligence to Impact," to life.

IT Brief UK reported that the partnership places the technology group alongside one of men's tennis's best-known season-ending events. The report said NTT DATA will use the tournament to show how AI, data and related systems can generate performance insights and support decision-making under pressure. IT Brief UK said the announcement reflects a wider trend in professional sport, where tournaments, teams and governing bodies use technology partnerships to enhance fan experiences and collect more detailed information on athlete preparation and match play. The report said tennis has become a testing ground for data-led analysis, with systems used across officiating, broadcast coverage and training. IT Brief UK said the demonstrations will place tools used in industrial and operational settings into a consumer-facing environment, linking them to measurable human activity rather than back-office processes.

NTT DATA is a $30+ billion business and technology services leader serving 75% of the Fortune Global 100. It describes itself as one of the world's leading AI and digital infrastructure providers, with capabilities in enterprise-scale AI, cloud, security, connectivity, data centers and application services. As a Global Top Employer, NTT DATA has experts in more than 70 countries. NTT DATA is part of NTT Group, which invests over $3 billion each year in R&D. NTT DATA said it will continue to build on these efforts, using sport as a platform to demonstrate how AI and technology can enhance human potential and create meaningful impact beyond sport.

NTT DATA said the partnership reflects its belief that intelligence comes not only from AI and technology, but also from human expertise and deep industry understanding. It said what matters is how these strengths are brought together to create meaningful impact for clients and society. NTT DATA offers clients access to a robust ecosystem of innovation centers as well as established and start-up partners. The company said its consulting and industry solutions help organizations and society move confidently and sustainably into the digital future. NTT DATA said it is committed to accelerating client success and positively impacting society through responsible innovation.

stories.Headline: CrowdStrike executive urges verifiable identities and runtime traceability for AI agents
stories.Summary:
Erik Gustavson, vice president of product and engineering for continuous identity at CrowdStrike, wrote in a sponsored Dark Reading article published on November 17, 2026, that AI agents run on endpoints with real privileges, reading and writing files, calling tools and pulling software packages, and that they behave non-deterministically, so the same prompt can take two different paths. He said much of the AI safety conversation centers on the model and its guardrails, which he called critical but only part of a bigger picture, and he noted that NIST's recent design tenets for agent identity call for separating an agent's reasoning from the systems that decide what it is allowed to do. He argued that guardrails alone cannot contain an agent with broad standing access to production. Gustavson wrote that when an agent takes an unexpected action, security teams need to know exactly what happened, which systems were affected and on whose authority it acted, and that auditors and regulators will ask for proof. He said answering those questions requires a continuous record linking prompts to the processes spawned, files opened, connections made and packages pulled, kept outside the agent's reach so it cannot erase its tracks, captured at runtime on the endpoints where agents execute and connected to enforcement so harmful actions can be stopped as they happen.

He cited attackers who in August 2025 published poisoned npm packages that hijacked victims' own AI command-line tools to steal credentials, to which CrowdStrike responded across more than 90 affected customers, and he noted adversaries break out from initial access in as little as 27 seconds. He also cited the CrowdStrike 2026 Global Threat Report warning that adversaries may compromise trusted agents to create malicious insiders. On responsibility, Gustavson wrote that agents routinely skip the onboarding that gives a new employee an identity and a role, because a developer or business user turns one on, it inherits that person's privileges and it starts working. He said traditional identity providers were built to manage human access rather than autonomous software, and that each agent needs its own verifiable identity built on open standards like SPIFFE rather than a borrowed human credential or a shared service account.

He recommended that organizations discover every agent across the fleet, sanctioned or unsanctioned, tie each to the responsible human or service, apply least privilege for only as long as the job lasts, and pursue zero standing privilege with continuous evaluation of identity risk, agent behavior and runtime context so access can be adjusted or revoked when conditions change. Gustavson addressed the argument that AI adoption should slow until every risk is understood, and he argued the opposite, comparing good brakes to what lets a car drive fast. He said organizations that can see and govern agent behavior will deploy more agents in more workflows sooner than competitors stuck in pilot mode, and that slowing down hands an advantage to adversaries and nation-states who have no intention of waiting. He concluded that guardrails will keep getting better and should, but that organizations should assume an agent will eventually do something nobody intended, so before any agent gets the keys it needs runtime traceability, an identity and controls that can take those keys away the moment risk changes.

Articles.Title: AI Agents Need Identities and Runtime Traceability - Dark Reading

stories.Headline: TARSBOT and Aptiv partner to develop and scale industrial embodied AI robots for smart manufacturing
stories.Summary:
TARSBOT and Aptiv signed an agreement to deepen their strategic collaboration on embodied AI. This event took place on November 16, 2026, in the city of Shanghai. The signing occurred during the 9th China International Import Expo, which is known as the CIIE. Both companies agreed to work together to advance industrial robotic systems. This partnership focuses on the development and deployment of embodied AI technology.

Aptiv expects to deploy 100 TARSBOT A-Series industrial robots by the end of 2026. These robots cover 33 application scenarios and 8 manufacturing process categories, including flexible assembly. The parties plan to achieve mass production in 2026 using high-performance computing platforms. A larger fleet of 1,000 units is targeted with support from the Jiading District Government. The first batch of robots is already operating at an Aptiv smart factory.

The two companies are responsible for validating applications within real industrial environments. They stated that production insights will support the iterative development of the AI World Engine. This AWE system serves as the general-purpose foundation model for TARSBOT embodied AI. The partners aim to combine end-to-end AI capabilities with established engineering expertise. They believe this combination will support efficient and reliable deployment at a large scale.

Manufacturers worldwide are affected by a growing demand for intelligent automation and supply-chain efficiency. These companies see embodied AI as an important force for advancing next-generation productivity. The collaboration aims to demonstrate that scalable deployment can be validated in practical settings. Aptiv provides the intelligent power distribution solutions and computing platforms for the robots. These platforms support core functions like motion control, perception, and decision-making.

The companies have already been working closely to develop China's first industrial embodied AI robot fleet. The first phase of this project is currently being implemented at an Aptiv production site. This initial work focused on adapting robots to manufacturing requirements and real production processes. The signing at the CIIE marks a more systematic and scaled phase of their cooperation. This background establishes the foundation for their expanded strategic agreement in Shanghai.

TARSBOT and Aptiv will now use China's manufacturing environments to connect robotic systems with applications. They intend to provide a scalable industrial reference for expanding AI across additional scenarios. This effort aims to create broader opportunities for smart manufacturing on a worldwide scale. The articles leave open the specific timeline for the 1,000 unit fleet deployment. They also do not specify the exact date for the start of mass production.

stories.Headline: Asean members sign grid pact to share clean power and back regional AI growth
stories.Summary:
All eleven Asean member states signed an enhanced memorandum of understanding in Manila earlier this week. This pact to build the Asean Power Grid entered into force on Sunday, November 15, 2026. The agreement aims to create an integrated regional electricity network to share clean power across borders. It seeks to strengthen supply security and smooth the adoption of intermittent renewable energy resources. This regional effort occurs as the COP31 conference in Turkey presses governments to speed up electrification.

The deal anchors cross-border interconnections, multilateral power trade, and financing for subsea cables and overland lines. It complements the APG Financing Initiative involving the Asean bloc, World Bank Group, and Asian Development Bank. Asean estimates it will require 764 billion US dollars for transmission and generation investment through 2045. The Philippines, which concluded its 2026 Asean chairmanship, faces bottlenecks in its Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao grids. These domestic issues persist despite a liberalised wholesale market and a green energy option programme.

Energy Secretary Sharon Garin stated the enhanced MOU brings commitment to resilience, innovation, and partnership into focus. She stressed the importance of attracting multilateral and private capital to support these regional energy goals. Robert Cooke of the GRA said policymakers can mobilise data centres as a force for renewables. He argued that hyperscalers have a direct commercial stake in funding grid upgrades to secure green electricity. This investment would also shield server farms from the risks posed by extreme weather events.

Rexor Amancio of the GRA warned that data centres might displace green power from other regional users. He noted that using standard annual certificates could drive up fossil gas and increase prices for everyone. More than nine in ten Philippine business leaders say their country is overly reliant on fossil-fuel imports. This reliance is the highest among 18 economies surveyed by E3G, the GRA, and We Mean Business. Data centre operators and corporate buyers are affected by permitting delays and congested transmission lines.

The region wants to be an AI hub, but grids still run largely on coal and gas. Global data centre electricity consumption rose 17 per cent in 2025, with AI facilities surging 50 per cent. Data centres accounted for roughly 40 per cent of corporate renewable power-purchase agreements signed globally last year. Some builders are installing onsite gas turbines because of multi-year connection queues, according to BloombergNEF reports. The International Renewable Energy Agency has a COP31 green data centre programme to prove electricity is local.

The immediate test is turning digital infrastructure investments into fresh renewable generation, storage, and transmission projects. Hyperscalers are being pressed to act as anchor customers for new geothermal, wind, and solar projects. Regulators are under pressure to close accounting loopholes that allow companies to claim 100 per cent renewable status. The pact could determine if the data centre sector accelerates green transitions or locks in fossil-fuel demand. The articles leave open whether the region can close the gap between ambition and system infrastructure.

Articles.Title: Asean Power Grid deal raises stakes for regional AI boom - The Business Times

stories.Headline: Calif Research uses OpenAI Codex to find Java4Shell flaw in one hour
stories.Summary:
The article reports that in November 2026, Dark Reading published a Reporters' Notebook video on vulnerability hysteria in the AI era, discussing the fallout from recent high-severity flaw disclosures. The piece cites Java4Shell, CVE-2026-114938, a 9.2 CVSS flaw in OpenJDK's Base64 decoder unearthed in one hour using OpenAI's Codex by Calif Research. It also cites NGINX2Root, CVE-2026-123007, a 9.2 CVSS critical integer underflow vulnerability affecting nginx HTTP/2 discovered by Rapid7 MDR. The article recalls PHP2Shell, two critical PHP vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, discovered by Calif and rated 9.2 on the CVSS scale. The video features TechTarget Cybersecurity's Alissa Irei, Cybersecurity Dive's David Jones, and Dark Reading's Fahmida Y. Rashid.

The PHP2Shell flaws were caused by out-of-memory corruption and stale global state errors, enabling unauthenticated remote attackers to execute arbitrary code on Web servers without credentials or prior access. The disclosure process was rocky and marked by accidental leaks on X, and many organizations preemptively pulled websites and critical services offline. The anticipated wave of machine-speed exploits failed to immediately materialize during what the article calls "Black October." Researchers demonstrated unauthenticated remote code execution in widely deployed enterprise tools like Keycloak and Jenkins, prompting CISA to call for immediate patching. Java4Shell has no universal exploit, so attackers must consider each application's memory layout and timing, how Base64 is used, and take application-dependent steps.

The article states that a CISO's primary responsibility is not to unilaterally order costly operational shutdowns or carry sole accountability for business risk. It says the CISO should clearly communicate technical and operational risks to executive leadership equipped to weigh security threats against business continuity. It says staying calm, focusing on risk-based prioritization, and adhering to core security fundamentals remain the most effective defenses against modern threats. Rashid said the discussion would cover scary security vulnerabilities and the lessons about how they are disclosed. Irei said PHP is in use in, she thinks, 70% of the world's websites.

Jones said he thought it was absolute chaos and was still trying to understand exactly what happened last month. He said the initial rollout of the patch and the disclosure were more than a little rocky and the hype was a moving target. He said major institutions all over the world preemptively took their sites offline because they had no way of triaging the potential fallout in time. He said there was a lot of bad code in a lot of the proofs of concept and it never quite amounted to the emergency it was set up to be. Irei said you don't want to be the organization that is the Wikipedia entry for the big one.

Rashid noted that with Log4j it was three days before proofs of concept started appearing, and there was a sense that those three days no longer exist. Jones said maybe we are better prepared but we don't want to get into a situation where we are crying wolf ahead of time. He asked whether Black October was deserved and said he has seen worse. Irei said there is a big question mark around sophisticated machine-speed AI-enabled attacks that we are not seeing yet. The article says complex exploit paths, hardware dependencies, and flawed proof-of-concept code mean severe flaws do not automatically lead to immediate compromises, even when attackers use AI.

The article says the pressure on cybersecurity teams to patch critical vulnerabilities is reaching a boiling point, exacerbated by incessant coverage and rapid-fire disclosures of AI-discovered bugs. It says constantly shuttering operations or broadcasting catastrophe can create early-warning fatigue, akin to ignored national weather alerts. It says that leaves organizations numb when a genuine emergency strikes. It says last month it was PHP2Shell and this week it is Java4Shell and NGINX2Root. It says the video examines whether the industry is falling victim to communal panic.

The article directs readers to learn more in the video and to check out other Reporters' Notebook episodes for insights and coverage from across Informa TechTarget's network of cybersecurity sister sites. It says the transcript was edited for clarity, readability, and length by Informa TechTarget's internal AI assistant and human editors. It says readers should watch the video for the full experience. Jones said we are still trying to get to the bottom of exactly what took place and how we can avoid some of the exaggerated threat. The article leaves open exactly what happened last month and whether there was an initial overreaction.

Articles.Title: Navigating Vulnerability Hysteria in the AI Era - Dark Reading

stories.Headline: Chinese AI stocks fall as US administration plans to block data center equipment imports
stories.Summary:
Investors sold off Chinese artificial intelligence hardware exporters and hyperscalers on November 18, 2026, as signs of tougher United States technology curbs emerged. This market decline occurred ahead of a scheduled meeting between Chinese leader Xi Jinping and United States President Donald Trump. The downturn followed the removal of Jensen Huang as chief executive officer of Nvidia after Republicans lost the United States midterm election. These events pushed China's stock benchmark toward its lowest levels since mid-2025.

The Trump administration intends to block imports of Chinese data center equipment despite opposition from American technology firms. The Federal Communications Commission previously sought to ban new models of Chinese optical transceivers due to national security concerns. Nvidia now assumes it will have no data center chip sales to China, while Senator Tammy Baldwin introduced legislation to revoke the normal trade status of China. Consequently, the CSI300 and Shanghai Composite Index both fell roughly 0.4 per cent, and the Hang Seng Tech index dropped 1.5 per cent.

Louis-Vincent Gave of Gavekal Research stated that the downfall of Jensen Huang could have consequences extending far beyond the artificial intelligence sector. He noted that tighter financing might threaten the investment boom while political tensions reshape the relations between the two nations. Other affected companies included Alibaba, Tencent, and MiniMax, as well as optical parts makers Zhongji Innolight and Eoptolink. The latter two firms have seen their values drop more than 70 per cent from their peak levels.

President Trump met with leaders from Australia, Japan, and India in the Philippines on Tuesday before a trilateral meeting in Shenzhen. The Quad expressed grave concerns regarding economic coercion, although the group did not explicitly name China in its statement. While most tech stocks fell, the Star Chip Index rose 0.5 per cent on expectations that domestic chipmakers would benefit from restrictions. Gold stocks also tumbled nearly 5 per cent because of expectations that the United States would raise interest rates.

Articles.Title: China AI stocks, hyperscalers hit by signs of tougher US tech curbs - The Business Times
