stories.Headline: Commerce Department approves sales of over 879,000 AI chips to Chinese companies
stories.Summary:
The Commerce Department approved sales of over 879,000 AI chips to Chinese companies as of May 2026. Representative Brian Mast revealed this information on Thursday through documents released by the House Foreign Affairs Committee. The Bureau of Industry and Security handled these specific approvals for the sales. Some licenses were granted for sales to firms designated as Chinese Military Companies. These approvals occurred amid escalating scrutiny of chip exports to China.

The Bureau of Industry and Security licensed H200 sales to Alibaba, Tencent, ByteDance, and other Chinese firms. Between December and May, Nvidia and AMD made 3.4 million requests for AI chip sales to China. The U.S. government required a 25 percent cut of sales for H200 shipments to approved customers. License requests also included firms like Baidu, Tesla Shanghai, and suspected smuggling fronts Maginfra and New Matrix. The Commerce Department issued a rule on Monday to stop Chinese companies leasing computing power from third countries.

Representative Gregory Meeks said the administration put national security and the technology edge at risk. He stated that the Bureau of Industry and Security failed to enforce rules and requires rigorous oversight. A spokesperson for the bureau said licensing decisions resulted from consultation among multiple government agencies. Nvidia spokesperson John Rizzo said approvals had strict conditions and limited volumes before shipping stopped. AMD stated it maintains rigorous processes to ensure compliance with all U.S. export control laws.

Analyst Stacy Rasgon said the number of approved chips is not that many and is not surprising. He noted that the government approved about one out of every four requested sales. Analyst Patrick Moorhead said sales remained limited because Beijing did not approve large scale imports. Hunterbrook Media alleged that blacklisted IEIT Systems continued receiving newer AMD firmware for its servers. Lawmakers are questioning if Jensen Huang's relationship with a suspected spy jeopardized American AI dominance.

Export controls on AI chips started under the Biden administration in 2022, leading Nvidia and AMD to re-engineer chips. Jensen Huang resigned from Nvidia after news surfaced regarding extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy. Investigators suspect Megaspeed, a Singaporean company where Alice Huang was an executive until 2025, diverted chips to China. The House Foreign Affairs Committee used the Export Control Reform Act to justify releasing the export data. Nvidia reported 2.4 billion dollars in quarterly revenue from H200 and related chip sales in China.

Jensen Huang is scheduled for a closed door transcribed interview with three committees on December 1. Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter will appear before the panels on December 2. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and Huang have also agreed to testify before the Senate banking committee. Congress has called for new legislation to impose stricter export controls on sales to China and adversaries. The articles leave open whether the suspected smuggling fronts Maginfra and New Matrix will respond to comments.

stories.Headline: Trump administration restricts Chinese companies from accessing advanced AI chips via remote computing power
stories.Summary:
The Trump administration restricted Chinese companies from accessing advanced AI chips via remote computing power this week. These new rules were announced on Monday to make it harder for firms to rent overseas power. The administration also imposed stricter rules on chip shipments to five countries, including Singapore and Malaysia. These actions followed the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang last week. Huang admitted to an affair with Alice Huang, a businesswoman accused of ties to Chinese intelligence.

Overseas data centers providing large amounts of computing power to China must now obtain special licenses. The rules target remote access used by tech firms like Alibaba and ByteDance to use Nvidia chips. Alice Huang previously worked at Megaspeed, a Singapore based data center company suspected of smuggling chips. In 2024 and 2025, Megaspeed imported 136,000 AI chips into Malaysia and Indonesia. Roughly 50,000 of those chips were not accounted for in initial Nvidia inventory checks.

A White House spokesperson said the rule would crack down on the smuggling of advanced US SI chips. The spokesperson stated the goal is to ensure advanced chips go to US SI innovators first. They want to prevent these chips from going to Chinese shell companies. The administration felt compelled to demonstrate they had the situation under control after the scandal. This response followed the embarrassing cheating scandal involving the former Nvidia chief executive.

The restrictions affect US technology companies that may lose business from their Chinese customers. Federal Reserve Bank of New York researchers found that affected suppliers struggled to replace lost business. They estimate these restrictions wiped 130 billion dollars from the combined market value of those companies. The policies also hurt the profitability and employment of these American suppliers. Chinese firms like Huawei and DeepSeek are now finding ways to compete without American technology.

The Biden administration began this strategy in the fall of 2022 to choke off China's chip access. Washington used the Bureau of Industry and Security to lead enforcement of these complex export controls. This agency had a budget of only 235 million dollars in 2026 to fight smuggling. The Institute for Progress estimates China could have 1 million smuggled H100 chips by late 2026. For decades, the US only used export controls for specific military programs or blacklisted companies.

Washington is now regulating how Chinese companies use chips even when hardware never enters China. The government is moving from preventing the acquisition of chips to regulating their global usage. It remains unclear if the original restrictions have actually accomplished their goals of preserving technological leads. Assessing the precise impact of these policies on Chinese AI companies has proven to be difficult. The articles leave open whether this expanded control will successfully stop China's cutting edge development.

stories.Headline: Researchers propose Vision-as-a-Tool to let text-only agents offload visual reasoning
stories.Summary:
Haolin Yang, Wenshan Wu, Jin Jiang, Yu Cheng, Yan Xia, Ting Song, Yangyu Huang, Zhiliang Peng, Wenhui Wang, Hangbo Bao, Yuzhe Zhang, Wen-Da Wei, Tengchao Lv, Li Dong, Lei Cui and Furu Wei posted a paper titled Vision-as-a-Tool: Visual Harness for Multimodal Agentic Coding to arXiv on 20 November 2026. The paper argues that multimodal agentic coding needs strong visual reasoning to analyze observations and to evaluate the artifacts that agents generate. Current frameworks mostly rely on a Thinking-with-Images paradigm, in which agents depend on their own intrinsic vision to carry out visually grounded tasks. That architectural coupling creates a fundamental bottleneck, because agent performance stays strictly bounded by internal perceptual limits, and text-only agents lack native perception entirely.

The authors introduce the Vision-as-a-Tool paradigm, which reframes general-purpose multimodal large language models as callable external utilities rather than as the agent's own eyes. Earlier visual tool use merely manipulated images for an agent's intrinsic vision to read, whereas this approach lets text-only agents completely offload visual reasoning during agentic execution. Vision-capable agents can meanwhile augment their native perception on demand, and the authors instantiate the paradigm in VHarness, a unified framework driven by five atomic actions. They evaluate VHarness across Image-to-HTML, Image-to-SVG and Image-to-3D generation tasks, and the results show that it consistently improves visual fidelity and geometric accuracy for both text-only and multimodal coding agents.

The paper is listed under Artificial Intelligence and Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition, and its authors conclude that modularizing visual reasoning into callable utilities gives a flexible and scalable foundation for future agentic coding systems. The abstract does not assign responsibility for any failure to a named person or organization, and it reports no statements beyond the authors' own framing of the bottleneck and their proposed fix. The article also carries standard arXivLabs boilerplate describing a framework through which collaborators develop and share features on the site, and noting that arXiv works only with partners who adhere to its values of openness, community, excellence and user data privacy. The posting invites ideas for projects that would add value to the arXiv community through arXivLabs, but the articles give no further details on deployment, timelines or follow-up work.

stories.Headline: Nebius revenue grows 571% as analyst upgrades stock to strong buy
stories.Summary:
Nebius Group N.V. shares have fallen about 65% from their all-time high and roughly 45% since the author's last coverage, a decline the article attributes to a general sell-off in AI-related stocks. The author upgraded the stock from Buy to Strong Buy on November 19, 2026, arguing that Wall Street is overlooking the company's AI infrastructure platform and its inference software. In the third quarter, Nebius revenue grew 571% to $981 million, and the AI Cloud EBITDA margin reached 53%, supported by demand and higher pricing. The article also describes an algorithmic compute marketplace that adjusts offers for demand and lease duration, with current prices running 15% below estimated customer willingness to pay.

The company cut its fiscal 2026 revenue guidance to between $3 billion and $3.2 billion after third-party delays at Microsoft's New Jersey data center. More than half of the contracted capacity is expected by year-end, with the remainder scheduled for the second quarter of 2027. Fiscal 2027 capital expenditure guidance is $40 billion to $45 billion, against expected customer prepayments of $17 billion to $20 billion and $7.4 billion in cash. Asset-backed financing is anticipated to cover 75% to 85% of that capital expenditure, though the article says additional debt or equity issuance may still be needed.

The author, a risk management business analyst at a Greek bank, wrote the article himself and discloses a beneficial long position in Nebius shares through stock ownership, options or other derivatives. He states that he received no compensation for the article beyond Seeking Alpha and has no business relationship with any company mentioned. He argues that the sell-off overlooks the company's infrastructure, software and funding model, while noting that execution risk on the marketplace is high and that short-term leases may constrain growth in remaining performance obligations. The article says valuation sits near the low end of Nebius's one-year EV/Sales range, and it advises investors to watch how the guidance cut and the financing plan develop.

stories.Headline: Apple negotiates four to five year DRAM supply deal with Samsung Electronics
stories.Summary:
Apple is reportedly in advanced talks with Samsung Electronics to begin a long-term DRAM supply contract lasting four to five years, scheduled to start in the first half of 2027, according to The Korea Herald. Apple negotiates the multiyear DRAM supply deal with Samsung Electronics after it signs a separate agreement with SK hynix. Industry sources state on Thursday that Apple and Samsung have reached the final stages of talks on the four- to five-year agreement. The proposed deal guarantees minimum supply volumes, while market conditions determine the prices. The rush for supplies occurs as technology firms like Amazon and Google invest heavily in AI data centres, which drives demand for high-bandwidth memory and server DRAM.

SK hynix said last month that it had secured long-term supply agreements with 14 major global customers, covering more than half of its production capacity for 2027 and 2028. The contracts typically run for five years. Samsung said last month that it had signed LTAs with 10 major customers and was negotiating with another 10. Citing data from market researcher TrendForce, the report noted that server DRAM's share of total demand rises to 43 per cent this year from 38 per cent in 2025. Mobile DRAM's share drops to 32 per cent from 36 per cent, the report noted.

An industry source said that in the past memory makers adjusted supply volumes and prices to meet customers' demands. The source said that now that available supplies are limited, bargaining power has shifted to suppliers. The source added that as long as AI infrastructure investment continues, chipmakers are likely to use long-term contracts to secure more stable revenue. Another industry source said long-term contracts are about more than securing supplies in advance. The source said buyers now have to commit to longer-term purchasing plans to get the volumes they need.

Rival Micron Technology already includes price floors, ceilings, cash deposits, and take-or-pay clauses in its five-year contracts, which force buyers to pay for committed volumes even if they purchase less. No signs show Samsung's deal with Apple includes identical terms, while Micron's contracts highlight supplier leverage. Chipmakers prioritize higher-margin components, which leaves less capacity for conventional memory in smartphones and personal computers. For Samsung and SK hynix, long-term deals provide clearer visibility over future orders in a sector known for sharp price swings. Tight supply lets them demand firm commitments and shift downturn risks onto buyers.

Samsung Electronics and SK hynix have entered a sharp correction, with their share prices falling an average of 55% from their respective peaks. Kim Dong-won, head of research at KB Securities, said in a report on Nov. 18 that the recent decline in semiconductor stocks reflects excessive fear. He explained that uncertainty surrounding changes in Nvidia's leadership and the U.S. Democratic Party's stance on AI regulation had fueled concerns about a slowdown in investment after 2028. Global hedge funds have also reduced their exposure to AI-related semiconductor stocks, while short-selling volumes have approached their highest level since 2016. KB Securities projected that demand for server DRAM and enterprise solid-state drives would increase by 56% and 54%, respectively, in 2027 from the previous year.

From 2027 to 2028, actual memory supply is estimated to meet only 60% to 70% of customer demand, meaning suppliers may be unable to meet 30% to 40% of the memory volumes customers require. Samsung Electronics and SK hynix are projected to generate a combined operating profit of 1,777 trillion won in 2026 and 2027, according to KB Securities. Samsung Electronics is projected to account for 1,022 trillion won, while SK hynix is expected to contribute 755 trillion won. KB Securities expects AI investment to translate into stronger memory demand, while limited capacity additions and long-term supply agreements are likely to help memory manufacturers maintain their pricing power. Kim emphasized the need to distinguish short-term supply-demand imbalances from the structural earnings outlook.

stories.Headline: Victoria Song tests Apple Watch Siri Recap feature for two weeks
stories.Summary:
Victoria Song tested the Siri Recap feature for two weeks on an Apple Watch. She is a senior reviewer for The Verge who reports on wearable technology. The testing occurred around November 19, 2026, to evaluate the new AI tool. Song compared this Apple feature to the Amazon Bee Frontier during her trial. She wanted to see if the experience felt less dystopian than other devices.

The feature requires an Apple Watch Ultra 4 or a 2026 Apple Watch S11 chip. Users must manually opt in because the tool is not turned on by default. Customization allows recording at specific places, like an office, between 1 and 2PM on weekdays. Recaps self-destruct after one, three, or seven days unless the user saves them. Processing happens locally or through Apple Private Cloud Compute to protect user privacy.

Apple presents the tool as a backup notetaker for students or parents at conferences. The company says the feature helps users remember better and stay more present. Apple claims the secure exclave in the S11 chip is inaccessible to third parties. They state that Siri does not train on the user's voice for privacy. This design choice prevents the AI from learning everything about the user's life.

Song found the tool mostly useless outside of a few specific work scenarios. She noted that bystanders may feel uncomfortable when a watch takes notes on them. The AI struggled to discern conversations, mistakenly summarizing TikTok videos about sepsis and bikinis. Song mentioned that her therapist suggested she throw the Amazon Bee Frontier away. She felt that relying on AI for judgment calls was an unsettling experience.

The articles explain that ambient listening is meant to jog memories for the user. Apple designed Siri Recap to be a minimalist, privacy-first alternative to the Amazon Bee. This hardware requirement means the feature cannot work on any older Apple Watch models. Unlike Live Rewind, this tool has no audio chime to signal that recording started. Users must explicitly disclose to people around them that the device is recording.

Song will continue to evaluate if the benefits of AI summaries outweigh the costs. The articles leave open whether users will accept the need for ethical disclosures. It remains unclear if Apple can improve the AI's ability to discern actual conversations. The text does not say if Apple will add an outward recording indicator. Song concludes that this technology may not be the answer for jogging memories.

stories.Headline: IBM and Confluent launch time-series foundation models for real-time forecasting
stories.Summary:
IBM and Confluent launched time-series foundation models on November 18, 2026, to provide real-time forecasting and anomaly detection. These models allow businesses to turn continuous records of change into decisions while the signals still matter for outcomes. The system uses Apache Flink to apply semantic intelligence to streaming data, making outputs available to responsible people. This technology extends the concept of foundation models from text and images to numerical data by learning general patterns. These tools help organizations avoid training separate models for every single data series by providing a common starting point.

The models run natively on CPUs in the cloud and on premises using Confluent Cloud or Confluent Platform. They have achieved more than 50 million downloads and include a family of four different foundation models. The Streamhouse architecture uses five capabilities, which are connect, stream, process, govern, and query, to serve business context. Lightning Tables provide low-latency access to current states, while Flink prepares data and invokes the forecasting and anomaly functions. These tools operate across manufacturing, retail, banking, and airlines to keep production lines in spec and detect unusual activity.

IBM and Confluent stated that their models reduce the need for dedicated GPU infrastructure by running on standard CPUs. They explained that pretrained models scale development by reducing the need to maintain separate models for each individual series. The providers noted that forecasts can incorporate recent observations as part of a streaming workflow based on pipeline configurations. They claimed that routing signals closer to decisions allows teams to combine them with business context and human judgment. These capabilities help businesses avoid making decisions based on outdated or inconsistent information from periodic batch processes.

Retail teams are affected as AI_DETECT_ANOMALIES compares sales readings with expected ranges to identify causes for low stock. Category planners use AI_FORECAST to produce 28-day forecasts with P10 to P90 ranges to calculate product reorder points. Bank fraud teams use time-series signals to compare payments with a card's recent history to request additional authentication. Execution desks use PatchTST-FM to forecast trading volume for the next 30 minutes to pace large 100,000-share orders. Reliability engineers use TSPulse to produce representations of time-series windows to search for similar historical patterns across equipment.

The articles explain that businesses generate continuous records through machine readings, payments, sales, orders, and changes in inventory. In ice cream production, engineers currently rely on QA lab measurements taken after tubs are already filled. This delay means hours of production may need rework if a warm day changes the process before results appear. The Streamhouse addresses this by continuously capturing and governing current business context to support applications and AI agents. This background shows that traditional systems often update at different times, leading to risks when acting on old data.

Next, the TTM model will read SCADA telemetry every 10 minutes to forecast product quality four hours ahead. Operators can then approve recommended freezer draw temperature and airflow setpoints to reduce rework and lower energy use. The system can be applied to other industrial equipment like ovens, dryers, kilns, and mills for proactive processes. The articles leave open how these models will integrate with other large language models and specialized machine learning systems. They do not specify the exact costs for enterprises to implement these native functions in the Confluent Cloud.

stories.Headline: Reson8 open sources Rumble-2-Flash speech recognition model supporting over 40 languages
stories.Summary:
Reson8 open sourced the Rumble-2-Flash speech recognition model on November 18, 2026. This open model uses 0.5 billion parameters to support more than 40 different languages. It can process one hour of audio in roughly half a second when using full batches. The system competes with larger models and provides control over fillers, numbers, and forced languages.

The model requires the Qwen3-ASR architecture and works with vLLM or Transformers without needing a forked runtime. It was created by distilling a larger production model called Rumble-2 using a method called on-policy distillation. This process used GOLD to merge different tokenizers so the student model could learn from its own mistakes. On the Open ASR Leaderboard, it achieved a 6.6 percent error rate for English and a 6.96 percent average across nine other languages.

The team at Reson8, including Mark t Hart, Eustache Le Bihan, and Eric Bezzam, released the weights under the Apache 2.0 license. They stated that the model is on par with NVIDIA's Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe, which has 30 billion parameters, on a 302-hour call-centre benchmark. The developers noted that the model is available through their API and on the Hugging Face Hub. They encouraged the community to share what they build and suggest changes for future versions.

stories.Headline: Foreign investors dump over 1.4 trillion won in AI shares and push the Kospi below 5,000
stories.Summary:
A brutal sell-off of AI stocks hit Wall Street on Thursday, November 5, 2026, causing global markets to feel significant downward pressure. Foreign investors dumped more than 1.4 trillion won in shares, which pushed the South Korean Kospi index below the 5,000 mark. This market crash erased the previous day's gains, which had been the best for the US stock market in three months. The sell-off was led by companies tied to the buildout of AI data centres and impacted various global indexes. The Kospi closed at 4,968.48 on Tuesday, marking its first time below 5,000 in roughly nine months.

The S&P 500 fell 4.4 per cent to 7,353.73, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average sank 1,833.06 points to 51,523.06. The Nasdaq composite tumbled 5.5 per cent to 24,315.00, falling 11.9 per cent below its all-time high set in October 2026. Nvidia fell 9.3 per cent, Advanced Micro Devices tumbled 17.3 per cent, and CoreWeave sank 9.8 per cent in New York. GE Vernova dropped 7.5 per cent, and the PHLX Semiconductor Sector Index plunged 5.3 per cent on Monday in New York trading. Japan's Nikkei 225 sank 1.8 per cent, and London's FTSE 100 dipped 0.4 per cent after Bank of England rate hikes.

Wall Street analysts and hedge fund managers expressed concern that the era of the no-brainer AI trade has finally ended. Anthony Bozza of Lakewood Capital Management called it unbelievable that many hedge funds decided to chase the exact same thing. Jay Jacobs from BlackRock stated that the current concentration in AI makes diversification harder to achieve than investors may realize. Peter Berezin of BCA Research suggested that AI might make companies more productive without necessarily making them more profitable. Andrew Goldberg of Nomura Asset Management warned that investors do not fully understand their total exposure to AI risks.

Retail investors in Korea continued buying AI stocks, with Nvidia topping their list with net purchases of 420.41 million US dollars. The National Pension Service of Korea held Nvidia as its largest US equity portfolio share at 7.34 per cent in Q3. Public pension funds in the US saw AI-related holdings reach 38.5 per cent in June, representing 9 to 11 per cent. Samsung Electronics lost 3.3 per cent and SK hynix lost 1.96 per cent as the AI investment boom faced intense scrutiny. Many voters across political parties expressed wariness about AI and the power bill increases caused by new data centres.

The market had been swinging for months due to high borrowing costs and fears that AI stock prices were bubbles. The S&P 500's worst day occurred since Donald Trump introduced Liberation Day tariffs in April 2025, which shook markets worldwide. The PHLX Semiconductor Sector Index has lost 34.3 per cent since its June peak, signaling a bear market for those stocks. Hedge funds specializing in technology stocks lost an average of 12.6 per cent by October after a period of growth. AI hardware stocks made up 40 per cent of Morgan Stanley's hedge fund client portfolios on a net basis.

Investors are now herding into US Treasury bonds, with the 10-year yield falling to 4.84 per cent from 4.90 per cent. PGIM is reviewing AI risks across 1 trillion dollars in bonds and loans to see if debt repayment is possible. The MSCI Global Intelligence Index estimates that global companies most directly exposed to AI hold at least 25.3 trillion dollars. It remains unknown how a slowdown in data centre construction will affect the purchase of AI chips and electricity services. Articles leave open when the global energy industry will return to normal and how the war with Iran ends.
